title: Proposal: Add `Coordinates` class to handle np arrays that describe coordinates
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We're starting to see some real usability issues when operating on bare numpy arrays describing sets of coordinates:
* Array shape inconsistencies (3, N) (N, 3) #438 
* Dimensionality inconsistencies (3, N, 1) and (N, 3, 1)
* Cryptic coordinate access, e.g. (indexing a numpy array with `.T[[0, 2]]` to get the x and z coordinates
* Inconsistencies with clockwise / counter-clockwise sets of coordinates #482 

## Proposed solution

I propose to introduce a `Coordinates` class, which will wrap `np.array`, providing only a handful of attributes and methods, designed exclusively to facilitate interaction with sets of coordinates, enforcing dimensionality, shape, and CCW upon instantiation.

My call would be: (3,N) and CCW by default (`.T` and `.reverse()` would allow the user to switch between these with ease anyway).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26097289/144566537-0f65da55-9238-4340-a025-107c47ca315a.png)

Note that `.xyz` would be the result of a bare call to `Coordinates`, so it is not necessary as an attribute. We .also need to have `Coordinates.T` behave just like a numpy array (along with probably a few other array views).

I'm sure yet whether sub-classing `np.ndarray` is the way forward, but it could be. The downside would be inheriting a whole bunch of functionality that may confuse the namespace, apart from implementation issues like have to add a whole bunch of dunder methods to get instantiation and array views to work correctly. If we agree, I'd probably start on a minimum working implementation without sub-classing.

In terms of integration, I would make a `Coordinates` instance from any wire discretisation operation. They will also no doubt get used elsewhere, but not for CAD creation. 

## Alternative solutions

We could standardise the dimensionality of arrays and just live with the coordinate access on a numpy array.

## Additional context

This was the original use-case for the BLUEPRINT `Loop` class, which admittedly grew out of hand because it was being used to make CAD and a whole bunch of other stuff. In the long-term, I also see this class as potentially replacing `Loop` in some of the places where they are still used in BLUEMIRA, such as in the `equilibria` module. I would strive to keep `Coordinates` as small as possible though, so anything that operates on `Coordinates` e.g. intersections, cutting, etc. would just return a new set of coordinates, and not add methods to the class. `rotate` and `translate` methods are perhaps a grey area, it's just I know they will be used. Plotting could be provided by the already existing `PointsPlotter`

I know Ivan will not be a big fan of this.. but we have spoken in the past of having classes for scalar and vector fields, and I see no reason not to have one for coordinates too. This is now addressing some real usability issues, in my opinion. Shadowing a numpy array should allow for the same behaviour as previously, but with a standardisation of array shape.

Thoughts @DanShort12 @fabrizio-franza @je-cook ?

title: FW power fraction reformulation for double null
body:
## Description of issue

The current power sharing in the FW and the particle flux power sharing as 4 fraction. 
Power conservation however sets the fractions sum must be one.

This is done through a posteriori test.

## Proposed solution

A much better way is to only have for fraction and no test *a posteriori* test:
- `f_sol_top`: To/bottom power fraction (the sum of the inboard and the outboard divetor leg)
- `f_sol_in_top`: fraction of the energy flowing to the top that goes on inboard
- `f_sol_in_bot`: fraction of the energy flowing to the top that goes on inboard

Remove the test that is now fulfulled by definition.

Best regards     
Seb

title: `Component.plot_2d` does not have args or kwarg. Plots do not have axis labels
body:
## Describe the bug
When build a component in x-y, I cannot choose the plot the component onto the x-y plane, and instead get a blank plot.

I am being mislead by `Plottable.plot_2d` which has a signature:

`    def plot_2d(self, ax=None, show: bool = True, *args, **kwargs) -> None:`

It then calls it's Plotter's `plot_2d` which uses the `BasePlotter`'s `plot_2d` with the signature:
`    def plot_2d(self, obj, ax=None, show: bool = True):`

In other words, my args and kwargs that I consistently try and use are being thrown away. A similar but different issues exists in `.plot_3d`.

When I do plot a component, the plot itself does not contain the axis labels or units.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
```python
from bluemira.geometry.parameterisations import PrincetonD
from bluemira.base.components import PhysicalComponent

p = PrincetonD().create_shape()
p2 = p.deepcopy()
p2.rotate(base=(0, 0, 0), direction=(1,0 ,0), degree=90)

c1 = PhysicalComponent("xz", p)
c2 = PhysicalComponent("xy", p2)

c2.plot_2d(plane="xy")
```

will give you:

```python
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
~/code/bluemira/bluemira/builders/pf_coils.py in <module>
      9 c2 = PhysicalComponent("xy", p2)
     10 
---> 11 c2.plot_2d(plane="xy")

~/code/bluemira/bluemira/display/plotter.py in plot_2d(self, ax, show, *args, **kwargs)
    757             The axes that the plot has been displayed onto.
    758         """
--> 759         return self._plotter.plot_2d(self, ax=ax, show=show, *args, **kwargs)
    760 
    761     def plot_3d(self, ax=None, show: bool = True, *args, **kwargs) -> None:

TypeError: plot_2d() got an unexpected keyword argument 'plane'
```

Of "course", if I want to do this, I have to do:

```python
from bluemira.geometry.parameterisations import PrincetonD
from bluemira.base.components import PhysicalComponent

p = PrincetonD().create_shape()
p2 = p.deepcopy()
p2.rotate(base=(0, 0, 0), direction=(1,0 ,0), degree=90)

c1 = PhysicalComponent("xz", p)
c2 = PhysicalComponent("xy", p2)

c2.plot_options.plane = "xy"
c2.plot_2d()
```

which may be the recommended behaviour, but I am getting deceived every time by the claim that `Component.plot_2d` takes kwargs. It doesn't.

## Expected behaviour

I expect that plotting components should be intuitive, and not mislead the user into thinking it works a particular way when it doesn't. I expect that the plots show labels with units on them.

- OS: Ubuntu 18.04
- Branch: develop

## Describe the bug

Plasma currents obtained by integration over the toroidal currents, as calculated directly from the `psi`, `ffprime` and `pprime` profiles in .`eqdsk` and `.json` outputs in `FIESTA,` are inconsistent with the output plasma current `cplasma` reported in the same files.

This may be because scaling to maintain the total plasma current is applied directly to the toroidal plasma currents in Bluemira, rather than the `ffprime` and `pprime` profiles, which are left unchanged after initialisation in a `CustomProfile` object.

Bluemira appears to use the total plasma current to rescale toroidal currents at every calculation of `jtor`, so otherwise remains self-consistent from provided inputs.

## Expected behaviour

Total plasma current in output data should be self consistent between the reported value and those calculated directly from psi and profile data.

title: Add support for start and end tangencies when using `make_bspline`
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Sometime when making a BSplineCurve, it can be very useful to set the start and end tangencies.

## Proposed solution

Add arguments and associated handling for them in `make_bspline` in `bluemira.geometry.tools.py`

## Alternative solutions

I think I had something for this in BLUEPRINT, but it delved quite deep into PythonOCC/OCC... this is in BLUEPRINT/geometry/cadtools.py

```python
def points_to_bspline(
    pnts,
    deg=3,
    periodic=False,
    tangents=None,
    scale=False,
    continuity=GeomAbs_C2,
    tol=TOLERANCE,
):
    """
    Makes a BSplineCurve from an x, y, z array of points

    Parameters
    ----------
    pnts : list or numpy array
        array of x, y, z points
    deg : integer
        degree of the fitted bspline
    periodic : Bool (default=False)
        If true, OCC.GeomAPI_Interpolate will be used instead of the
        GeomAPI_PointsToBspline. Curve tangent vectors can then be enforced at
        the interpolation pnts
    tangents : array (default=None)
        list of [x, y, z] tangent vectors to be specificied at points:
        if only 2 tangents are specified, these will be enforced at the
        start and end points, otherwise tangents should have the same length
        as pnts and will be enforced at each point.
    scale : bool (default=False)
        Will scale the tangents (gives a smoother Periodic curve if False)
    continuity : OCC.GeomAbs.GeomAbs_XX type (default C2)
        The order of continuity (C^0, C^1, C^2, G^0, ....)

    Returns
    -------
    crv : OCC.Geom.BSplineCurve
    """
    if not periodic and (tangents is None):
        crv = _points_to_bspline(pnts, deg=deg, continuity=continuity)
    else:
        typer = TColgp_HArray1OfPnt
        try:
            pnts = point_array_to_TColgp_PntArrayType(pnts, typer).GetHandle()
        except AttributeError:
            pnts = point_array_to_TColgp_PntArrayType(pnts, typer)
        interp = GeomAPI_Interpolate(pnts, periodic, tol)
        if tangents is not None:
            n_tangents = tangents.shape[0]
            if n_tangents == 2:
                interp.Load(gp_Vec(*tangents[0, :]), gp_Vec(*tangents[1, :]), scale)
            else:
                tan_array = TColgp_Array1OfVec(1, n_tangents)
                for i in range(1, n_tangents + 1):
                    tan_array.SetValue(i, gp_Vec(*tangents[i - 1, :]))

                tan_flags = TColStd_HArray1OfBoolean(1, n_tangents)
                tan_flags.Init(True)  # Set all true (enforce all tangents)
                try:
                    tan_flags = tan_flags.GetHandle()
                except AttributeError:
                    pass
                interp.Load(tan_array, tan_flags, scale)
        interp.Perform()
        crv = interp.Curve()
    return crv
```

## Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: Generalise interface for run_systems_code
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Currently we look for a configuration key `"process_mode"` in run_systems_code to determine the run mode. As part of the generalisation of some of the bluemira design/build logic, we are looking to nest configuration for each build stage. As such it would be cleaner to align on a common `"mode"` key within each design stage for which a run mode is relevant.

e.g. the following:

```python
build_config = {
    ...,
    "process_mode": "run",
   ...,
}
```

Would become:

```python
build_config = {
    ...,
    "PROCESS": {
        ...,
        "mode": "run",
        ...,
    },
    ...,
}
```
## Proposed solution

Modify the `run_systems_code` interface to look for the `build_config` as supplied for the relevant design stage. The run mode would then be determined by the `mode` key within that config, and we could also simplify the rest of the `process.Run` interface to just take in the `params` and the subset of the `build_config` for that stage.

## Alternative solutions

We can work around this by translating the nested config values into the flat values needed for the current PROCESS interface (and probably will do this in the short term).

## Additional context

Not assigning this, but @je-cook - might be relevant or worth discussion for the external codes interfacing work that is on-going?

title: Write JSON of systems to volume names and IDs.
body:
## Description

The purpose of this PR is to provide sufficient information to automate the creation of a DAGMC file from the STP assembly file. To be specific, DAGMC requires the addition of material groups in metadata, so it is necessary to make explicit which volumes in the CAD file correspond to a single material. 

Had it not been for a bug in Cubit, it may have been possible to extract such information from the CAD name data (c.f. #522 ). The specific bug, which is detailed [here]( https://forum.coreform.com/t/missing-volume-metadata-after-stp-import-in-solid-with-void/1324), has the consequence that name data is not imported when the solid is hollow. This is the case for e.g. the PF coil casing. Since we cannot depend on this data being present, I decided to write these grouping in a JSON file. Although less elegant, this approach potentially allows for more future flexibility if it transpires we should not be grouping by system, but by another metric (e.g. a material tag?).

## Key assumptions
- The Volume ID corresponds to the ID in the STP file; this is internally generated by OCC and corresponds to the ordering in which the volumes are added to STP file.
- The list of volume names and IDs are grouped against the system they come from. This is based on the assumption that such systems may correspond to homogenised materials. If this is not the case then the mappings will need to be adjusted accordingly.

Add a keep-out zone constraint to the TF coil WP shape optimisation problem that comes from the TFCoilsBuilder x-z component.

title: Proposal: Reorganise displayers and plotters
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

The various displayers and plotters currently reside in the `display` module. This often leads to circular imports because the functionality to retrieve the plotter e.g. `_get_plotter_class` needs to know about the classes that can be plotted/displayed. This inter-dependency suggests that in reality the plotter/displayer should be in the same module as the thing that it can plot / display.

## Proposed solution

Move the specific plotters and displayers into the same modules as the things that are being plotted/displayed. It should also be possible to register the class to be plotted / displayed with its corresponding plotter without hard coding them into `_get_plotter_class` and equivalents. This could be done with a decorator to explicitly say what plotter should be used for the class being registered.

## Alternative solutions

We could probably achieve something similar by using `__init_subclass__` and directly assigning the plotter / displayer class to the class to be plotted/displayed.

## Additional context

This will likely leave the `display` module as even smaller than it currently is. It may then be worth considering moving this into `base` to reduce the number of separate modules that we have. However, as `displayer.py` depends on an external code (cadapi) this could be bad for future independence of core modules from external codes (although so much will depend on the cadapi that perhaps this is less of a concern).

title: Default parameter mapping should be empty dict not None
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Currently we set undefined mappings to None. This is somewhat less user friendly than setting the default to be an empty dict, so we may want to change that default. This would mean one can do:

```python
param.get_param(param_name).mapping["PLASMOD"] = ParameterMapping(plasmod_name, send=True, recv=False)
```

Rather than:

```python
param.get_param(param_name).mapping = {"PLASMOD": ParameterMapping(plasmod_name, send=True, recv=False)}
```

In particular the former case allows the mapping to be created in the same way whether other mappings exist or not, while the latter could lead to unexpectedly removing mappings for other codes.

## Proposed solution

Change the default value of mapping on parameters to be {} rather than None.

title: Strategy for avoiding circular imports
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We have quite a lot of cases now where it is easy to introduce circular imports and have collectively spent quite a bit of time resolving cases where they do get introduced. I'm putting this in as a place to collect some thoughts on how we might improve that. Some points of reference:

- We have some cases where inter-dependent functionality are quite far apart, so these should probably be brought together.
- In some cases we have imports that are only used for type hinting. There are some strategies to resolve this (using `TYPE_CHECKING` to only run the imports if a type checker is running), and we should get in the habit of applying these.
- In my experience most of the circular imports boil down to loading something in a `__init__.py`. I personally like being able to see the module for an import when it's being used, but perhaps removing these imports and importing from the module may help in the short term.

## Proposed solution

To be discussed.

## Alternative solutions

To be discussed.

title: Implement Coordinates interface
body:
## Linked Issues

Closes #438, #482 

## Description

Threads in `Coordinates` as the result of a wire discretisation. Effectively give you a (3, N) numpy array, with a couple of extra features.

## Interface Changes

`make_polygon` now takes (3, N) and (N,3) arrays as well as lists of 3-D points, or a dict of `{"x": [...], "y": [...], "z": [...]}` coordinates.

The only change (which was significant due to our many tests with 3-point polygons) is that a (3, 3) array will now be assumed to be a (3, N) array, i.e. the reverse of what it was previously.

The result of `BluemiraWire.discretize` now returns `Coordinates` which is a (3, N) array and not a (N, 3) array as previously.

`Coordinates` can now be accessed via `.x`, `.y`, `.z`, `.xy`, `.xz`, `.yz`, and we have `.points` or `.T` or for (N,3) lists and arrays, respectively.

`Coordinates` are not set as CCW by default, but one can set them to CCW w.r.t. an axis (defaults to the best-fit planar-axis).

`GeometryParameterisation.create_array` removed

title: Plasmod mock run fails
body:
## Describe the bug
Running Plasmod in mock, the following error is returned:
`bluemira.codes.error.CodesError: PLASMOD error: Abnormal paramters, possibly dtmax/dtmin too large`

## Steps to reproduce
Run `bluemira/examples/codes/run_plasmod_examples.py` using `build_config['mode'] = 'mock'`

## Expected behaviour

Read the mock plasma outputs stored in the working folder without error

## Environment (please complete the following information)

- OS: [macOs]
- Version [10.13.6]
- Branch [develop]

## Additional context
The problem is probably due to the fact that the variable `i_flag` is not correctly initialized during mock-Teardown.

## Possible solution
In `codes/plasmod/api.py` modify `Teardown._mock` function as follows
```python
    def _mock(self):
        """
        Mock plasmod teardown
        """
        self.io_manager = Outputs()
        self.io_manager.i_flag = 1
        self.io_manager.read_output_files(
            Path(self._run_dir, self.parent.setup_obj.output_file),
            Path(self._run_dir, self.parent.setup_obj.profiles_file),
        )
        self.prepare_outputs()
```

title: Make it possible to view a specified number of sectors when displaying Reactor CAD model
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

When we show the CAD of a `Reactor`, we're very often not going to want to see the fully patterned CAD model with `n_TF` sectors. Such a model, when fully populated, will be aesthetically pretty boring: we'd just see the full radiation shield building and nothing else.

In BLUEPRINT, we usually used to show either a 1/2 or 3/4 view, in which fully revolved components (typically the plasma and the PF coils) were also segmented somehow to a fractional view (I can't remember how).

We should re-establish the ability to be able to view `n` sectors of a `Reactor`.

## Proposed solution

Open to ideas here. Some initial thoughts:

*  add an `n_sectors` argument to `Reactor.show_cad`
*  add an `n_sectors` or similar to `component.display_cad_options`

Fully revolved components (e.g. plasma) may need to be sectored. Note that in BLUEPRINT we found it was a serious pain in the ass to pattern the transparent plasma without getting faces at each sector.

@DanShort12

## Alternative solutions

In BLUEPRINT we also had an admittedly convoluted way of showing different numbers of sectors for different `ReactorSystems` which had the potential to create some cool models.

## Additional context

Honestly, there's probably something to be said for having one "display" CAD model, and one that gets used in the real world. The real world one we might not want to have sectors - effectively boolean fusing together all the sectors to reduce the number of surfaces and volumes that are treated. That's probably something for another issue.

title: Radiation model
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Add models to calculate the radiation source term from a `Equilibrium` and a set of impurities and radiative loss functions:
* Core radiation (1-D PROCESS core radiation but extrapolated to 2-D, see https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0920379615302891 and https://doi.org/10.13182/FST11-A11650)
* SOL radiation (2-D model based on the two point model, see https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0741-3335/39/6/001 and http://data.lib.hutech.edu.vn/mucluc/d456afd00c0e17e699ebb904ac38de19.pdf)

## Proposed solution

* Implement the aforementioned models in the `radiation_transport` module.
* As a first pass, do not implement as a base `Solver` class
* Extract the flux surface "access" presently in `AdvectiveTransportSolver` and move in to a new utility class, that is used in both `AdvectiveTransportSolver` and `SOLRadiationTransportSolver` (future PR)

## Proposed API

Inputs:
* `Equilibrium`
* Impurity radiative loss functions from ADAS (use PROCESS for now)
* Parameters:
 * Impurities concentrations (from PROCESS)
 * Separatrix power
 * Transmission sheath coefficient (e.g. 25 eV)
 * Hydrogen ionisation temperature
 * Ideal detachment temperature for the target
* Problem settings (gaussian/exp decay, etc.)

Outputs:
* Radiation source term as an array based on a set of points OR a set of psi_norm values
* Radiation source term (including core and SOL contributions) as a function (disgestable by CHERAB - needs investigation, potential need to interpolate)

Try and maintain the same API (in terms of methods) for the core and SOL radiation models

Updated following discussion:

```python
# User-facing solver should include core and SOL source terms
solver = RadiationSourceTermSolver(parameters, eq: Equilibrium, *args, **kwargs)

# Calculate source term at specific input points
radiation_at_points = solver.calculate_source_at_points(x: np.ndarray, z: np.ndarray)

# Calculate source term at specific psi_norm values
points, radiation_at_points = solver.calculate_source_at_psi_norm(psi_n: np.ndarray)
```

title: Simplify method to get default mappings for external code
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We used to have hard-coded mappings for PROCESS in the `Configuration` class and correspondingly in json parameterisation files. It certainly makes sense for these default mappings to now be owned by the code to which they correspond, but one side effect of this is that the mappings are now further away from where a user might look to know what the defaults would be.

## Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a common method across external code APIs to extract the default mappings and possibly apply them to a `Configuration` to generate the full parameterisation if that code were to be used. Ideally it would be possible for a user to define their own default parameterisations and extract them in the same (or at least similar) way.

## Alternative solutions

When making `Configuration` instances to use for a design, or for writing to json, we could just access the mappings for the external code and build them in (like is currently done in the EU-DEMO example) but it would be cleaner to have some unified way to do this.

title: Seperate optimisation logic from the rest of the build logic
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Currently the optimisation process for some BLUEPRINT components is mixed in with other steps needed to build a complete reactor component. This is a problem if one wishes to create a reactor component without optimisation, e.g. when recreating the results of a previous run by reading it in.

## Proposed solution

Separate the optimisation logic into callbacks stored on the reactor class. A user can then configure them to do different jobs, or none at all, as needed. By setting a callback to `None` optimisation can be turned off while the rest of the build should work as expected.

## Alternative solutions

Boolean logic and if-statements could be used for this but it would result in more complicated control-flow and be less flexible. Inheritance and overriding of methods could be used instead of callbacks but has more overhead in terms of how much code is required.

## Additional context

The STEP reactor project wants to be able to recreate a complete Reactor object in memory by reading in the output from a previous run. This will allow users to write scripts that produce any additional output they want, without having to modify the output methods in the main project.

Release notes

Sourced from pyparsing's releases.

pyparsing 3.0.7

  • Fixed bug #345, in which delimitedList changed expressions in place using expr.streamline(). Reported by Kim Gräsman, thanks!

  • Fixed bug #346, when a string of word characters was passed to WordStart or WordEnd instead of just taking the default value. Originally posted as a question by Parag on StackOverflow, good catch!

  • Fixed bug #350, in which White expressions could fail to match due to unintended whitespace-skipping. Reported by Fu Hanxi, thank you!

  • Fixed bug #355, when a QuotedString is defined with characters in its quoteChar string containing regex-significant characters such as ., *, ?, [, ], etc.

  • Fixed bug in ParserElement.run_tests where comments would be displayed using with_line_numbers.

  • Added optional "min" and "max" arguments to delimited_list. PR submitted by Marius, thanks!

  • Added new API change note in whats_new_in_pyparsing_3_0_0, regarding a bug fix in the bool() behavior of ParseResults.

    Prior to pyparsing 3.0.x, the ParseResults class implementation of __bool__ would return False if the ParseResults item list was empty, even if it contained named results. In 3.0.0 and later, ParseResults will return True if either the item list is not empty or if the named results dict is not empty.

    # generate an empty ParseResults by parsing a blank string with
# a ZeroOrMore
result = Word(alphas)[...].parse_string("")
print(result.as_list())
print(result.as_dict())
print(bool(result))

    add a results name to the result
    

    result["name"] = "empty result"
print(result.as_list())
print(result.as_dict())
print(bool(result))

    Prints:

    []
{}
False

    []
{'name': 'empty result'}
True

    In previous versions, the second call to bool() would return False.

  • Minor enhancement to Word generation of internal regular expression, to emit consecutive characters in range, such as "ab", as "ab", not "a-b".

  • Fixed character ranges for search terms using non-Western characters in booleansearchparser, PR submitted by tc-yu, nice work!

  • Additional type annotations on public methods.

Changelog

  • Fixed bug #350, in which White expressions could fail to match due to unintended whitespace-skipping. Reported by Fu Hanxi, thank you!

title: Codes cleanup and finish generic wrapper
body:
## Description

This does a bit of cleanup of some of codes and does some renaming to enable generic wrappers that came up from discussions and thoughts on Friday. Code interfaces can now be loaded on the fly from anywhere with builtin location in `bluemira.codes` the preference.

## Interface Changes

`plot_PROCESS` has been renamed to `plot_radial_build` and `run_systems_code` to `systems_code_solver`. `systems_code_solver` now returns the solver object which needs to be run externally (allowing flexibility and reruns)

## Description of issue / requirement to address

I personally struggle with the (base, axis, angle) formulation of a `BluemiraPlane`, because it doesn't really do what I expect, even if that may be correct as a method. 

We already have `from_3_points` as a classmethod, enabling one to make a plane from 3 points, but I'm now running into the situation where I already know the rotation matrix of a plane and I just want to make a `BluemiraPlane` from a 4 x 4 matrix. 

This is possible in FreeCAD's `Placement`.

## Proposed solution

Add a classmethod to `BluemiraPlane` allowing the user to make a `BluemiraPlane.from_matrix`

## Alternative solutions

Part of the point of outsourcing the heavy lifting to FreeCAD is to not have to maintain these geometry transformations which honestly are pretty fiddly and different conventions for edge cases are possible. BUT, the alternative would be to write (or re-write) some of these transformations.

title: Check flux surface geometry conventions and write documentation describing the geometry in detail
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Upon adding the squareness calculation, I remember that I had put another problem aside; that of the actual flux surface geometry definitions.

Many parameters are technically defined w.r.t. some centre point, the location of which is sometimes debatable. Most textbooks (e.g. Stangeby, Freidberg, Ariola + Pironti) do tend to define things like elongation and triangularity w.r.t to pure geometry, but it is at least in some cases considered reasonable to define these w.r.t. the magnetic axis.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26097289/151349515-40efa48d-854c-4ab6-9c78-985e03a310ec.png)

I've asked Hartmut Zohm for advice because I have to say, I'm a bit worried about different definitions being used in different places.

## Proposed solution

At the moment `ClosedFluxSurface` has a bit of a mixed set of definitions here, so these must be standardised.

We also need to add some clear documentation describing these with some images.

title: Sorting of coils breaks if name contains multi-digit numbers
body:
## Describe the bug

The `CoilGroup.sort_coils()` method can't deal with coil names containing multi-digit numbers, interpreting names like `CS10` as being before `CS7`.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from bluemira.equilibria.coils import CoilGroup, Coil
coils = [
    Coil(5, 5, 0, dx=1.0, dz=1.0, name="CS_2"),
    Coil(5, 5, 0, dx=1.0, dz=1.0, name="CS_10"),
]
sorted_coils = CoilGroup.sort_coils(coils)
sorted_names = list(sorted_coils)
assert sorted_names[0] == "CS_2"
assert sorted_names[1] == "CS_10"
```

## Expected behaviour

I'd expect the coils to be sorted in "[natural order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_sort_order)"

## Environment (please complete the following information)

- OS: Ubuntu 18.04
- Branch: develop

title: Change flux surface convention and add documentation
body:
## Linked Issues

Requires #646 
Closes #654 

Flux surface geometry now defined w.r.t. the centroid of the fictional reference ellipse, in line with most textbooks and seemingly general convention. Still an outstanding doubt related to the definition of upper and lower triangularity and vertical Shafranov shift where I've made an opinionated decision that they should be w.r.t. to the average vertical position of the radial extrema. 

It's still pretty debatable on how to handle the vertical position of the "centroid" however, especially when one considers things like NT, SF, or the general funky case where the elevations of the minimum and maximum radii of the shape are not nearly equal.

## Description

Clears up the convention on calculation of geometric flux surface quantities and adds documentation.

title: Bump black from 21.12b0 to 22.1.0
body:
Bumps [black](https://github.com/psf/black) from 21.12b0 to 22.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from black's releases.

22.1.0

At long last, Black is no longer a beta product! This is the first non-beta release and the first release covered by our new stability policy.

Highlights

  • Remove Python 2 support (#2740)
  • Introduce the --preview flag (#2752)

Style

  • Deprecate --experimental-string-processing and move the functionality under --preview (#2789)
  • For stubs, one blank line between class attributes and methods is now kept if there's at least one pre-existing blank line (#2736)
  • Black now normalizes string prefix order (#2297)
  • Remove spaces around power operators if both operands are simple (#2726)
  • Work around bug that causes unstable formatting in some cases in the presence of the magic trailing comma (#2807)
  • Use parentheses for attribute access on decimal float and int literals (#2799)
  • Don't add whitespace for attribute access on hexadecimal, binary, octal, and complex literals (#2799)
  • Treat blank lines in stubs the same inside top-level if statements (#2820)
  • Fix unstable formatting with semicolons and arithmetic expressions (#2817)
  • Fix unstable formatting around magic trailing comma (#2572)

Parser

  • Fix mapping cases that contain as-expressions, like case {"key": 1 | 2 as password} (#2686)
  • Fix cases that contain multiple top-level as-expressions, like case 1 as a, 2 as b (#2716)
  • Fix call patterns that contain as-expressions with keyword arguments, like case Foo(bar=baz as quux) (#2749)
  • Tuple unpacking on return and yield constructs now implies 3.8+ (#2700)
  • Unparenthesized tuples on annotated assignments (e.g values: Tuple[int, ...] = 1, 2, 3) now implies 3.8+ (#2708)
  • Fix handling of standalone match() or case() when there is a trailing newline or a comment inside of the parentheses. (#2760)
  • from __future__ import annotations statement now implies Python 3.7+ (#2690)

Performance

  • Speed-up the new backtracking parser about 4X in general (enabled when --target-version is set to 3.10 and higher). (#2728)
  • Black is now compiled with mypyc for an overall 2x speed-up. 64-bit Windows, MacOS, and Linux (not including musl) are supported. (#1009, #2431)

Configuration

  • Do not accept bare carriage return line endings in pyproject.toml (#2408)
  • Add configuration option (python-cell-magics) to format cells with custom magics in Jupyter Notebooks (#2744)
  • Allow setting custom cache directory on all platforms with environment variable BLACK_CACHE_DIR (#2739).
  • Enable Python 3.10+ by default, without any extra need to specify --target-version=py310. (#2758)
  • Make passing SRC or --code mandatory and mutually exclusive (#2804)

Output

  • Improve error message for invalid regular expression (#2678)
  • Improve error message when parsing fails during AST safety check by embedding the underlying SyntaxError (#2693)
  • No longer color diff headers white as it's unreadable in light themed terminals (#2691)
  • Text coloring added in the final statistics (#2712)
  • Verbose mode also now describes how a project root was discovered and which paths will be formatted. (#2526)

Packaging

  • All upper version bounds on dependencies have been removed (#2718)
  • typing-extensions is no longer a required dependency in Python 3.10+ (#2772)
  • Set click lower bound to 8.0.0 as Black crashes on 7.1.2 (#2791)

title: Bump coverage[toml] from 6.2 to 6.3
body:
Bumps [coverage[toml]](https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy) from 6.2 to 6.3.
Release notes

Sourced from coverage[toml]'s releases.

6.3

  • Feature: Added the lcov command to generate reports in LCOV format. Thanks, Bradley Burns. Closes issues 587 and 626.
  • Feature: the coverage data file can now be specified on the command line with the --data-file option in any command that reads or writes data. This is in addition to the existing COVERAGE_FILE environment variable. Closes issue 624. Thanks, Nikita Bloshchanevich.
  • Feature: coverage measurement data will now be written when a SIGTERM signal is received by the process. This includes https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.Process.terminate, and other ways to terminate a process. Currently this is only on Linux and Mac; Windows is not supported. Fixes issue 1307.
  • Dropped support for Python 3.6, which reached end-of-life on 2021-12-23.
  • Updated Python 3.11 support to 3.11.0a4, fixing issue 1294.
  • Fix: the coverage data file is now created in a more robust way, to avoid problems when multiple processes are trying to write data at once. Fixes issues 1303 and 883.
  • Fix: a .gitignore file will only be written into the HTML report output directory if the directory is empty. This should prevent certain unfortunate accidents of writing the file where it is not wanted.
  • Releases now have MacOS arm64 wheels for Apple Silicon, fixing issue 1288.

title: Equilibrium analysis tools
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

This is a general issue to gather requirements for a set of functionality relating to equilibrium queries. Once we have a fairly complete list of required functionality, we can then discuss implementation and do the work.

At present a wide range of different tools are available in the `equilibria` module and in the BLUEPRINT `StreamFlow` object. The latter has some functionality which is not present in the new module, but is set to be deprecated.

## Proposed solution

In my head, there are three generic categories of request for information on an `Equilibrium` object:
* Calculation of some floating point value, integral or otherwise: (e.g. psi at some point, internal inductance of the plasma, flux surface elongation)
* Queries as to where some physical feature lies in space: (e.g. finding the O, X-points, finding the LCFS, finding a flux surface based on some criterion)
* Queries related to the structure of the core plasma: (e.g. profiles, values plotted on a per-flux-surface basis)
Implement functionality for the following equilibrium queries:

At present, these bits of functionality are strewn about between `equilibria/physics.py`, `equilibria/find.py`, and `equilbria/flux_surfaces.py`. I propose to compile a list of desired functionality, restructure these tools in a clearer way, and implement any missing features.

## Desired functionality

| Description of functionality| Exists in `equilibria` |Name(s)  | New name | 
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | 
| Finding the O and X points| ☒ |`find_OX_points`, `eq.get_OX_points()` | |
| Finding the last closed flux surface | ☒ |`find_LCFS_separatrix`, `eq.get_LCFS()` | |
| Finding the separatrix | ☒ |`find_LCFS_separatrix`, `eq.get_separatrix()` | |
| Finding the separatrix legs | ☒  | `get_legs`| |
| Finding a flux surface from a specified point | ☒  | `find_flux_surface_through_point`| |
| Finding a flux surface(s) from a normalised psi vale| ☒  | `find_flux_surf`, `eq.get_flux_surface()`| |
| Finding the inboard midplane point | ☐  | | |
| Finding the outboard midplane point | ☐  | | |
| Calculating the radial field due to the equilibrium and coils | ☒  | `eq.Bx()`| |
| Calculating the vertical field due to the equilibrium and coils | ☒  | `eq.Bz()`| |
| Calculating the poloidal field due to the equilibrium and coils | ☒  | `eq.Bp()`| |
| Calculating the toroidal field (as 1/x estimate - no knowledge of TF coils) | ☒  | `eq.Bt()`| |
| Calculating the plasma internal inductance | ☒  | `calc_Li`| |
| Calculating the normalised plasma internal inductance | ☒  | `calc_li`, `calc_li3`| |
| Calculating the plasma volume | ☒  | `calc_volume`| |
| Calculating the plasma energy | ☒  | `calc_energy`| |
| Calculating the ratio of plasma pressure to magnetic pressure | ☒  | `calc_betap`, `calc_beta_p`, `beta_p` [facepalm]| |
| Calculating the safety factor | ☒  | `eq.q()`, `ClosedFluxSurface.safety_factor()`| |
| Calculating the 3-D connection length | ☒  | `calculate_connection_length_flt`, `calculate_connection_length_fs`, `ClosedFluxSurface.connection_length()`| |
| Calculating the elongation of a flux surface | ☒  | `ClosedFluxSurface.kappa[upper, lower]`| |
| Calculating the triangularity of a flux surface | ☒  | `ClosedFluxSurface.delta[upper, lower]`| |
| Calculating the (outer) squareness of a flux surface | ☒  | `ClosedFluxSurface.zeta[upper, lower]`| |
| Calculate the field angle at a point | ☐  | | |

TO BE UPDATED as part of this issue


## Alternative solutions

We could carry on as is and add in pieces of functionality piecemeal, but we're already struggling with organisation and duplication of little helper functions and the like.

## Additional context

Quite a few people probably want to have a say in terms of what is required, so @hsaunders1904 @markj997 @DarioV86 @je-cook @alexanderianblair @DanShort12 , please feel free to comment on this issue.

title: Write initial first wall builder
body:
## Linked Issues
#642

## Description

Implements `FirstWallBuilder` class and adds the "First wall" component to the `EUDEMOReactor`.

Three builder classes have been implemented:
- `WallBuilder`: builds a closed wall shape, independent of divertor
- `DivertorBuilder`: builds the divertor components
- `FirstWallBuilder`: runs `WallBuilder`, cuts it off below the x-point, and uses `DivertorBuilder` to make a divertor in the gap.

Also added is the `MinimiseLength` geometry optimisation class, which minimises the length of a shape parameterisation with some constraints.

Some incomplete parts:
- Divertor targets are currently always vertical
- Divertor baffles are currently straight lines
- Only single-null plasmas with x-point at lower end are supported

Another note for reviewers, the function `bluemira.geometry.tools.find_point_along_wire_at_length` is currently implemented using discretisation. Is there a way to do this using primitives?

## Description of issue / requirement to address

We've come across an issue in #589 in which a `BluemiraFace` is created from an allegedly valid `BluemiraWire` but the resulting face is not valid. It was found that calling `.fix(float, float, float)` on this fixed the face.

Add a `fix_face` function in `_freecadapi.py` and use it (under the hood) when `BluemiraFace`s are created. Warn if the resulting face required fixing.

I am not proposing to make this a user-facing function for the time being.

## Alternative solutions

Haven't come across any good alternatives. Given that this can happen with a wire that is supposedly valid means we will need some form of detection and protection against these cases sooner or later.

title: Generalize the Optimization class to any statistical problem
body:
## Requirement to address

After a very nice review on the Optimization problem re-factor done by @alexanderianblair, it appeared that Sensitivity analysis, Incertainty propagation and data exploration (sampling) are all sharing very similar structures. They all need
- A list of input with variation bounds
- A figure of merit
- They potentially include constraints

A potential generalization is hence possible.

## Proposed solution

It may be good to have a StatisticProblem parent class from which the Optimizer/Optimizer problem classes are child. With for example a sensitivity analysis class linked with sampling algorithm from the SALib (https://salib.github.io/SALib/) library.

Best regards

Ref: @alexanderianblair, @CoronelBuendia

title: Boolean geometry operations on faces do not check for co-planearity and fail if the planes are flipped
body:
## Describe the bug

Strange errors occur if doing boolean operations on 2-D Faces which are not on the same plane, or have opposite normal vectors.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

Unfortunately you have to run the whole EUDEMO_reactor.py script and do some extract of geometry in the thermal shield builder at present in order to see this.

Geometry serialisation not yet implemented so can't just load up the geometries from files.

1. Run script EUDEMO_reactor.py in an interactive console on branch `matti/thermal-shield`
2. Run the following lines of code:
```python
from typing import List, Optional

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull

import bluemira.utilities.plot_tools as bm_plot_tools
from bluemira.base.builder import BuildConfig, Builder
from bluemira.base.components import Component, PhysicalComponent
from bluemira.base.config import Configuration
from bluemira.builders.EUDEMO.tools import circular_pattern_component
from bluemira.display.palettes import BLUE_PALETTE
from bluemira.geometry.error import GeometryError
from bluemira.geometry.face import BluemiraFace
from bluemira.geometry.plane import BluemiraPlane
from bluemira.geometry.tools import (
    boolean_cut,
    boolean_fuse,
    make_circle,
    make_polygon,
    offset_wire,
    revolve_shape,
    slice_shape,
)
from bluemira.geometry.wire import BluemiraWire

self = thermal_shield_builder
pf_xz = self._pf_kozs
x, z = [], []
for coil in pf_xz:
    bound_box = coil.bounding_box
    x_corner = [
        bound_box.x_min,
        bound_box.x_max,
        bound_box.x_max,
        bound_box.x_min,
    ]
    z_corner = [
        bound_box.z_min,
        bound_box.z_min,
        bound_box.z_max,
        bound_box.z_max,
    ]
    x.extend(x_corner)
    z.extend(z_corner)

# Project extrema slightly beyond axis (might be bad for NT) - will get cut later
x.extend([-0.5, -0.5])  # [m]
z.extend([np.min(z), np.max(z)])
x, z = np.array(x), np.array(z)
hull_idx = ConvexHull(np.array([x, z]).T).vertices
wire = make_polygon({"x": x[hull_idx], "y": 0, "z": z[hull_idx]}, closed=True)
wire = offset_wire(wire, self.params.g_ts_pf, open_wire=False)
pf_o_wire = offset_wire(wire, self.params.tk_ts, open_wire=False)

tf_o_wire = offset_wire(
    self._tf_koz, self.params.g_ts_tf, join="arc", open_wire=False
)

try:
    cts_inner = boolean_fuse(
        [BluemiraFace(pf_o_wire), BluemiraFace(tf_o_wire)]
    ).boundary[0]
except GeometryError:
   print("That should have worked")

print(pf_o_wire._shape.findPlane().Axis)  # [0, -1, 0]
print(tf_o_wire._shape.findPlane().Axis)  # [ 0, 1, 0]
```

## Expected behaviour

I expect a clear error message to be raised if the faces are not on the same plane. I expect a warning to be raised if the faces have opposite normal vectors, but the correct result to be returned nevertheless.

## Screenshots / Tracebacks
If you dig down into the FreeCAD layer you can see that the `removeSplitter` operation doesn't do anything, but that three faces are generated instead of one, which triggers a `GeometryError`.

  • #9404: Added extra documentation on alternatives to common misuses of [pytest.warns(None)]{.title-ref} ahead of its deprecation.
  • #9505: Clarify where the configuration files are located. To avoid confusions documentation mentions that configuration file is located in the root of the repository.

Trivial/Internal Changes

  • #9521: Add test coverage to assertion rewrite path.

pytest 7.0.0rc1 (2021-12-06)

Breaking Changes

  • #7259: The Node.reportinfo() <non-python tests>{.interpreted-text role="ref"} function first return value type has been expanded from [py.path.local | str]{.title-ref} to [os.PathLike[str] | str]{.title-ref}.

    Most plugins which refer to [reportinfo()]{.title-ref} only define it as part of a custom pytest.Item{.interpreted-text role="class"} implementation. Since [py.path.local]{.title-ref} is a [os.PathLike[str]]{.title-ref}, these plugins are unaffacted.

    Plugins and users which call [reportinfo()]{.title-ref}, use the first return value and interact with it as a [py.path.local]{.title-ref}, would need to adjust by calling [py.path.local(fspath)]{.title-ref}. Although preferably, avoid the legacy [py.path.local]{.title-ref} and use [pathlib.Path]{.title-ref}, or use [item.location]{.title-ref} or [item.path]{.title-ref}, instead.

title: Add EU-DEMO vacuum vessel builder
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Once we have builders for the first wall, breeding blanket, and divertors (in 2-D to start with), we will need a VacuumVesselBuilder.

This should be done with a simple offset from the blanket + divertor to get the inner silhouette, pinned to the radial build vector entries for the VV. Following this, we will need a variable thickness offset ranging from inboard to outboard, once again pinned to the radial build vector entries.

## Proposed solution
Add a new builder for the vacuum vessel poloidal cross-section, implement ports in a future PR.

Add a method to produce a variable thickness offset, which may be quite specific to the EU-DEMO vacuum vessel concept.

## Alternative solutions

We definitely need a builder.
Whether or not to use an offset versus some other method to produce the outer silhouette of the VV poloidal cross-section is debatable.

Sourced from prompt-toolkit's changelog.

3.0.28: 2022-02-11

New features:

  • Support format specifiers for HTML and ANSI formatted text.
  • Accept defaults for checkbox and radio list, and their corresponding dialogs.

Fixes:

  • Fix resetting of cursor shape after the application terminates.

3.0.27: 2022-02-07

New features:

  • Support for cursor shapes. The cursor shape for prompts/applications can now be configured, either as a fixed cursor shape, or in case of Vi input mode, according to the current input mode.
  • Handle "cursor forward" command in ANSI formatted text. This makes it possible to render many kinds of generated ANSI art.
  • Accept align attribute in Label widget.
  • Added PlainTextOutput: an output implementation that doesn't render any ANSI escape sequences. This will be used by default when redirecting stdout to a file.
  • Added create_app_session_from_tty: a context manager that enforces input/output to go to the current TTY, even if stdin/stdout are attached to pipes.
  • Added to_plain_text utility for converting formatted text into plain text.

Fixes:

  • Don't automatically use sys.stderr for output when sys.stdout is not a TTY, but sys.stderr is. The previous behavior was confusing, especially when rendering formatted text to the output, and we expect it to follow redirection.

title: Add `register_solver` and save input / output files for FPIs
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We need to be able to access solver information from solves that were used to generate a reactor. E.g. PROCESS and PLASMOD, which have FPIs, but also for other solvers (e.g. BoP) which have an API.

The solver information should be easily accesible.

Solvers may be run multiple times, and we need to store the inputs/outputs for those solvers, in particular for the FPI solvers.

## Proposed solution
For builders we do register_builder and get_builder, so we could do the same for solvers (or generalise the register/get for builders to something like register/get build_stage and include solvers in that). As a more future-looking change we probably also want to (perhaps optionally) store history information for builders/solvers - like we do for parameters.

## Alternative solutions

A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

## Additional context
Comes from some issues that cropped up in #636 and #707

title: Plotting the radial build from systems code run
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

It should be easy to plot the radial build of a reactor, resulting from a systems code run.

At present the PROCESS radial build plotting relies on some hacking of the OUT.DAT, because the radial build vector is not stored in variables.

## Proposed solution

We could reconstruct the radial build vector and makes some parameters for these.

Plotting the radial build is then a "view" of the reactors parameters, rather than plotting the solver per se.

## Alternative solutions

PROCESS could also output the radial build vector with some associated variable names we could map to.. maintaining a reconstruction of the radial build vector to mimic PROCESS is surely going to be difficult in the long run.


## Additional context

Probably needs to be actioned after #721

title: Removing shape parametrization default values
body:
## Description of issue

Default values have caused some issues in the past for STEP reactor as it cause unexpected behaviour. At best the code crashes and you know there is an issue. The worst case scenario is when the unknown defaut value bias the optimization problem without you knowing it.

`GeometryParameterisation` child classes all have default values for their 
`BoundedVariable`, and it has provent in the past a problematic feature.

Code snipet
``` python 

    def __init__(self, var_dict=None):
        variables = OptVariables(
            [
                BoundedVariable(
                    "x1", 4, lower_bound=2, upper_bound=6, descr="Inboard limb radius"
                ),
                BoundedVariable(
                    "x2",
                    14,
                    lower_bound=10,
                    upper_bound=18,
                    descr="Outboard limb radius",
                ),
                BoundedVariable(
                    "dz",
                    0,
                    lower_bound=-0.5,
                    upper_bound=0.5,
                    descr="Vertical offset from z=0",
                ),
            ],
            frozen=True,
        )
```

## Proposed solution

Get rid of the `BoundedVariables` default values and use directly `var_dict` to set them, that becomes non-optional.

Of course the keys have then to be checked and the relavant error message should be sent.

The error message could contain proposed values for the defauts to help the user setting them if he is in trouble doing so.

title: Add an abstract base class for solvers
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We currently support `FileProgrammableInterface` for integration with some external codes (PROCESS and PLASMOD). It would be helpful to generalise this interface to other internal and external interfaces so that we can expand to other use cases.

## Proposed solution

Add a `SolverABC` that can support the general interfacing for the setup/run/teardown approach. We probably need a bit more thought on where that abstract class should live (codes vs base). Also need a bit of thought around what the minimum implementation of such an interface would look like.

## Alternative solutions

We could also support a soft interface by checking whether the class being used supports setup/run/teardown.

## Additional context

This came up as part of the solver registration work but there are a bunch of other things that could be considered solvers that we will want to register (balance of plant, equilibria?, fuel cycle, ...) so it would be nice to have an interface that supports running any of those from a design (or potentially builder).

title: Implement variable thickness offset function
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

A function to generate a shape with a variable offset to another shape is required. The aim of the function is to enable building shapes with a variable thickness based on given offsets. This is required by components like blankets and the vacuum vessel.

A discretised version of this is implemented in `BLUEPRINT.geometry.offset.varied_angular_offset`. The functionality should be replicated using primitives.

The desired outcome is something along these lines:
* For a given planar wire, produce a variable thickness offset ranging from the inboard to the outboard about the mid-plane of the shape (centered at center of mass)
* Two thickness are specified: one on the inboard, one on the outboard
* The radius of the offset shape should never be less than the thickness at the midplane
* The transition of the offset should be continuous and smooth
* The poloidal angle at which the offset operation starts should be specified as an input
* Up-down symmetry about the mid-plane of the offset thickness may be assumed, but the shape itself may not be up-down symmetric
*

title: Dynamic bound evaluation
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Currently we can use the configuration to map parameters to variables in a `GeometryParameterisation`. However, this means that we don't know a priori what value a bound may have if it is to be defined relative to the initial value of a parameter.

## Proposed solution

Add dynamic evaluation (similar to materials properties) to `BoundedVariable`s. This would allow a variable to be defined like the below in configuration:

```python
variable_map = {
    ...
    "x1": {
        "value": "r_tf_out_centre",
        "upper_bound": "r_tf_out_centre * 1.5",
        "lower_bound": "r_tf_out_centre * 0.5",
    },
    ...
}

```

## Alternative solutions

We're currently creating individual parameterisation classes for specific cases. We could keep doing that but it is not so scalable.

## Describe the bug

The `center_of_mass` property on `BluemiraWire` is returning a FreeCAD `Vector` where it should be returning a `np.ndarray`.

```python
import numpy as np
from bluemira.geometry.tools import make_circle

circle = make_circle()
assert type(circle.center_of_mass) == np.ndarray
```

We may want to do a quick check that we're not accidentally exposing any other instances of FreeCAD types in the CAD API.

title: Removing flux surface that doesn't intersect the wall

title: Change magnetic constraints to magnetic targets
body:
Renamed for now. I think changing the name to 'targets' is good for a future PR, as it can be confusing to explain to new users that the MagneticConstraintSet in constraints.py is actually not used as constraints for the optimisation in the usual sense, but the set of targets for the objective function....

I'd be happier if 'constraints' were strictly used only in the OptimisationProblem sense, and that the field targets are renamed, so we can be clear in our documentation about what we're referring to as 'constraints' without the name clash muddying the waters. Nothing to stop the field targets being used as constraints of course, as you say, but I think they remain conceptually different. Should be a separate PR.

_Originally posted by @alexanderianblair in https://github.com/Fusion-Power-Plant-Framework/bluemira/pull/530#discussion_r818602737_

title: Make `GeometryOptimisationProblem` a sub-class of `OptimisationProblem`
body:
This feels like an alternative API to set up a general optimisation problem. It does get around some of the nastiness of e.g. `GeometryOptimisationProblem`, because different sets of constraints can be specified as inputs rather than hard-coded. I don't have a problem at all with a different API, but I am a little concerned that we're starting to have lots of different ways of doing things.

body:
Bumps [wrapt](https://github.com/GrahamDumpleton/wrapt) from 1.13.3 to 1.14.0.
Changelog

Sourced from wrapt's changelog.

Version 1.14.0

Bugs Fixed

  • Python 3.11 dropped inspect.formatargspec() which was used in creating signature changing decorators. Now bundling a version of this function which uses Parameter and Signature from inspect module when available. The replacement function is exposed as wrapt.formatargspec() if need it for your own code.

  • When using a decorator on a class, isinstance() checks wouldn't previously work as expected and you had to manually use Type.__wrapped__ to access the real type when doing instance checks. The __instancecheck__ hook is now implemented such that you don't have to use Type.__wrapped__ instead of Type as last argument to isinstance().

  • Eliminated deprecation warnings related to Python module import system, which would have turned into broken code in Python 3.12. This was used by the post import hook mechanism.

New Features

  • Binary wheels provided on PyPi for aarch64 Linux systems and macOS native silicon where supported by Python when using pypa/cibuildwheel.

title: Bump pytest from 7.0.1 to 7.1.0
body:
Bumps [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) from 7.0.1 to 7.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

7.1.0

pytest 7.1.0 (2022-03-13)

Breaking Changes

  • #8838: As per our policy, the following features have been deprecated in the 6.X series and are now removed:

    • pytest._fillfuncargs function.
    • pytest_warning_captured hook - use pytest_warning_recorded instead.
    • -k -foobar syntax - use -k 'not foobar' instead.
    • -k foobar: syntax.
    • pytest.collect module - import from pytest directly.

    For more information consult Deprecations and Removals in the docs.

  • #9437: Dropped support for Python 3.6, which reached end-of-life at 2021-12-23.

Improvements

  • #5192: Fixed test output for some data types where -v would show less information.

    Also, when showing diffs for sequences, -q would produce full diffs instead of the expected diff.

  • #9362: pytest now avoids specialized assert formatting when it is detected that the default __eq__ is overridden in attrs or dataclasses.

  • #9536: When -vv is given on command line, show skipping and xfail reasons in full instead of truncating them to fit the terminal width.

title: Remove reinitialise from builders
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We currently have a fair bit of complexity being introduced by trying to maintain state though reinitialisation of builder classes. This drives some complications in API, while at the same time not actively being used (or having a clear requirement until we have cases that repeatedly run a given build).

## Proposed solution

Remove reinitialise methods from builders.

## Alternative solutions

We could keep things as they are, but they will likely need to change anyway when we get round to having designs that repeatedly call a given build stage (such as via global optimisers).

## Additional context

Probably worth putting in an additional issue to cover versioning builders when called multiple times.

title: Emulate msh2xdmf functionality with options for 2-D meshing with specified plane and 3-D meshing.
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

The existing open-source (LGPLv3) functionality available at https://github.com/floiseau/msh2xdmf is presently used but brings with it a number of downsides. It has to be installed locally (not via pip) and means we need to check if it was installed prior to calling it.

It also only handles 2-D meshing in the x-y plane, and a lot of our 2-D meshing is likely going to be required in the x-z plane. There is a workaround for this, but it is a little undesirable.

## Proposed solution

Given the minimal overhead, we agreed to emulate this functionality, providing the necessary modifications and sparing us from import checks.

Add a MSH to XMDF converter in `mesh/tools.py`, crediting the authors of the original repository (and linking to it).

## Alternative solutions

We could continue to use it as it or get in touch with the developers and propose modifications directly.

## Additional context
It's likely that any dependencies changes (e.g. moving to fenics-X) could bring in further modifications. LGPLv3 license could however be problematic.

@ivanmaione

title: Add "display" attribute to `Parameter` class, to allow user to select units in applied to plots, tables and diagrams
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
When running each particular module, a user might be tempted to individually convert each parameter value into preferred units for plots, tables or diagrams; e.g. power flows in the Power Cycle displayed in MW instead of W.

## Proposed solution
Centralize this feature in the `Parameter` class, so that it can be used by every module, a new set of attributes should be created:
- **display**:           what is stored in `value`, but transformed to the units in `display_unit`
- **display_unit**:   units desired in plots, tables or diagrams

Ideally:
- the implementation should include a starting value of `None` in `default_unit`, so that no transformation is applied as a default.
- each module modifies internally the settings for default units for each parameter, that should only be applied during its own run.

title: Implement variable thickness offset function
body:
## Linked Issues

Closes #763 

## Description

Implements a variable offset function for `BluemiraWire`s. 

The function is implemented to offset wires in the xz-plane, but this could fairly easily be changed to any of the 2D planes. This will only sensibly work with convex shapes.

The function takes a minimum offset, maximum offset and two angles, between which the offset increases linearly between the minimum and maximum offset. 

It works by discretizing the wire in xz, taking the normals to the tangents at each point, then adding the offsets to the original points along the normal vectors. The new points are joined using a B-spline to make the new wire.

``` bash
for name, model_cls in models:
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

Here is the guilty function

``` python 
    def _validate_models(self, writer):
        models = [
            "iefrf",
            CurrentDriveEfficiencyModel,
            "i_tf_sup",
            TFCoilConductorTechnology,
        ]

        for name, model_cls in models:
            try:
                val = writer.data[name].value
            except KeyError:
                continue
            model = model_cls[val] if isinstance(val, str) else model_cls(val)
            writer.add_parameter(name, model.value)
```

There is two errors here:
- `models` is declared as a list and should be a dict instead (`.items()` shouls be added)
- The `Enum` value access does not function.

## Steps to reproduce

Simply read *PROCESS* inputs.

## Expected behaviour

No errors.

## Proposed solution

``` python
    def _validate_models(self, writer):
        """
        Function checking if the PROCESS writer option are supported.
        Calls the mapping Enum (Model) and verify if the chosen
        model number is present in it. Issue a warning otherwise.

        ARGUMENT
        --------
        writer:
            PROCESS writer object 
        """
        models = {
            "iefrf": CurrentDriveEfficiencyModel,
            "i_tf_sup": TFCoilConductorTechnology,
        }

        for name, model_cls in models.items():

            # Check only the model option set in the PROCESS output
            try:
                val = str(writer.data[name].value)
            except KeyError:
                continue
  
            if val.isdigit():
                 val = int(val)
                    
            model = model_cls[val] if isinstance(val, str) else model_cls(val)
            writer.add_parameter(name, model.value)
```

  • Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/jinja/milestone/12?closed=1

3.1.0

This is a feature release, which includes new features and removes previously deprecated features. The 3.1.x branch is now the supported bugfix branch, the 3.0.x branch has become a tag marking the end of support for that branch. We encourage everyone to upgrade, and to use a tool such as pip-tools to pin all dependencies and control upgrades. We also encourage upgrading to MarkupSafe 2.1.1, the latest version at this time.

  • Changes: https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/3.1.x/changes/#version-3-1-0
  • Milestone: https://github.com/pallets/jinja/milestone/8?closed=1
  • MarkupSafe changes: https://markupsafe.palletsprojects.com/en/2.1.x/changes/#version-2-1-1
Changelog

Sourced from jinja2's changelog.

Version 3.1.1

Released 2022-03-25

  • The template filename on Windows uses the primary path separator. :issue:1637

Version 3.1.0

Released 2022-03-24

  • Drop support for Python 3.6. :pr:1534

  • Remove previously deprecated code. :pr:1544

    • WithExtension and AutoEscapeExtension are built-in now.
    • contextfilter and contextfunction are replaced by pass_context. evalcontextfilter and evalcontextfunction are replaced by pass_eval_context. environmentfilter and environmentfunction are replaced by pass_environment.
    • Markup and escape should be imported from MarkupSafe.
    • Compiled templates from very old Jinja versions may need to be recompiled.
    • Legacy resolve mode for Context subclasses is no longer supported. Override resolve_or_missing instead of resolve.
    • unicode_urlencode is renamed to url_quote.

  • Add support for native types in macros. :issue:1510

  • The {% trans %} tag can use pgettext and npgettext by passing a context string as the first token in the tag, like {% trans "title" %}. :issue:1430

  • Update valid identifier characters from Python 3.6 to 3.7. :pr:1571

  • Filters and tests decorated with @async_variant are pickleable. :pr:1612

  • Add items filter. :issue:1561

  • Subscriptions ([0], etc.) can be used after filters, tests, and calls when the environment is in async mode. :issue:1573

  • The groupby filter is case-insensitive by default, matching other comparison filters. Added the case_sensitive parameter to control this. :issue:1463

  • Windows drive-relative path segments in template names will not result in FileSystemLoader and PackageLoader loading from drive-relative paths. :pr:1621

title: Support multiple build stages for a single component
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

At present a build stage in a reactor produces a component which is added to the component reactor tree.

For some components, the build sequence actually comes in multiple different build steps, scattered throughout the reactor build procedure. E.g. the thermal shield:

* build vacuum vessel
* build vacuum vessel thermal shield (VVTS)
* ...
* build PF coils
* build cryostat thermal shield (CTS)
* build ports (thermal shield ports)
* ...

IThe ThermalShield component should have the VVTS, CTS and ports as children.

At present this is not possible.

## Proposed solution
Have separate builders for each of the sub-components, and assemble them into the (e.g.) ThermalShield component.

For this we would need to have `Component.add_child` which can support `merge_trees=True`.

## Alternative solutions

We could also have a single builder that gets called multiple times with different build steps and signatures. This could get messy and is likely to be less modular.

## Describe the bug

``` python
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np

from bluemira.equilibria.file import EQDSKInterface

# Define tested file

# Load via eqdsk reader
reader = EQDSKInterface()
reader_dict = reader.read(file_path)

# Get reader qpsi and psi from 0 to 1
qpsi_reader = reader_dict["qpsi"]
qpsi_size = len(qpsi_reader)
psi = np.arange(qpsi_size) / float(qpsi_size)

# Plot qpsi reader
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(psi, qpsi_reader, '-r', label="Reader load")

EQ = Equilibrium.from_eqdsk(file_path, load_large_file=False)

# Plot qpsi Equilibrium
ax.plot(psi, qpsi_EQ, '-b', label="EQ load")
ax.set(xlabel=r"$\psi_\mathrm{N}$", ylabel=r"$q_\psi$")

# Add legend
ax.legend()

fig.canvas.draw()
```

Both profiles are expected to the exactly the same!

title: Vacuum vessel thickness inconsistencies with PROCESS
body:
## Describe the bug

This is more a note that we have to address a couple of little things surrounding the inboard and outboard vacuum vessel thickness `Parameters` `tk_vv_in` and `tk_vv_out`.

These are technically mapped to PROCESS, but PROCESS has a "shield" component which is not used in EU-DEMO, and for whatever reason is still seen in the outputs (or at least our mock JSON thereof).

We should remember to set the shield thicknesses in PROCESS to 0.0, such that our input VV thicknesses travel through PROCESS correctly and come out the other side with no knowledge of this shield component.

I don't know what the PROCESS variable names are anymore, off the top of my head it was `shldth` or something.

## Steps to reproduce

Run the EU-DEMO example file with PROCESS in mock and see that the vacuum vessel is too thin :)

## Expected behaviour
I would like to be able to run the build with the desired VV thicknesses (in both mock, read, and run). We might need to do the sums of the PROCESS vv and shield thicknesses in read if the shield thicknesses are not 0.0, or catch this somehow in the mapping.

title: Add EU-DEMO ports for RM scheme
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We need to have ports into the vacuum vessel to allow in particular for remote maintenance of the in-vessel components.

This requires a small reduced model to calculate in a crude way some of the IVC kinematics (in particular for the blanket segments). This should be used to create exclusion zones for the position of the PF coil positioning routine.

The ports should also be included in the CAD models of the VV, thermal shield, cryostat, and radiation shield.

## Proposed solution
Add a routine to calculate the size of the upper and lower ports based on remote maintenance considerations.

Add build stages for the ports to update the VV, thermal shield, cryostat, and radiation shield components

## Alternative solutions

N/A

title: Add in-vessel component segmentation for RM scheme
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We need to segment the in-vessel components in such a way that they may be extracted from the vacuum vessel via the ports.

## Proposed solution

Add build stages for the blankets and divertors, segmenting them as per RM requirements and the ports sizes (see #906 )

## Alternative solutions

A few different segmentations possible.. we'll start with the simplest one.

title: PROCESS v2.3.0 mappings are incorrect for the TF coil (and possibly elsewhere)
body:
## Describe the bug

PROCESS has finally changed how it represents the radial build of the TF coils, but unfortunately, due to some apparent changes in the meaning of some of the variables, this causes some errors in bluemira.

```
                                          Thickness (m)    Outer radius (m)
 Innermost edge of TF coil                    3.333           3.333                       
 Coil case ("nose")                           0.498           3.831   (thkcas)            
 Insertion gap for winding pack               0.010           3.841   (tfinsgap)          
 Winding pack ground insulation               0.008           3.849   (tinstf)            
 Winding - first half                         0.226           4.074   (dr_tf_wp/2-tinstf-t
 Winding - second half                        0.226           4.300   (dr_tf_wp/2-tinstf-t
 Winding pack insulation                      0.008           4.308   (tinstf)            
 Insertion gap for winding pack               0.010           4.318   (tfinsgap)          
 Plasma side case min radius                  0.060           4.378   (casthi)            
 Plasma side case max radius                  4.446           4.446   (r_tf_inboard_out)  
 TF coil dimensions are consistent
```
The ground insulation and insertion gap are now correctly separated, with the insertion gap only on one side. The thickness of the winding pack however seems to have a different definition to the previous value we were mapping to.

This causes the TF WP in bluemira to be very small (much smaller than PROCESS actually thinks it should be), probably because we are no longer mapping to the correct variable, or that we no longer need to reverse engineer the PROCESS TF coil build to get what we need out of it.

It's entirely possible that there are other inconsistencies or changes that we need to adapt to. Given that we're now pinning to v 2.3.0 by default, we need to act.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Using script 'examples/designs/EUDEMO/EUDEMO_reactor.py with PROCESS (v.2.2.0) note that the TF coil WP looks much too thin. 
2. With v2.3.0 it fails during the build of the TF coil with a deep OCCError.

## Expected behaviour

I'd like this script to run with v2.3.0 (at the very least) and for the mapping s to PROCESS to be correct.

title: Add an abstract base class for solvers
body:
## Linked Issues

Closes #759

## Description

Adds a `SolverABC` class.

The solver is intended to be general enough that any type of problem can run, be that an external code like PROCESS, or a Bluemira algorithm. 

I've included an example on how I propose the class could/should be used.

It's largely modelled on the `FileProgramInterface` class (which will need to be rejigged), using `Task`s that can be run in different "modes" (e.g., `RUN`, `MOCK`, `READ`).

Looking for some feedback on the design to begin with, then we can start moving existing solvers onto the new interface.

Notes:

- Another options is to pass constructed `Task`s into the solver's constructor. This would separate the concerns of construction

- I was a little torn on use of `*args, **kwargs` in the base class. I've opted to use dictionaries for now, but fundamentally that's the same thing as `**kwargs`, but doesn't portray that the overriding class can set their own inputs...

- Are all solvers going to require a setup, run, and teardown? If not, then we need to offer some way of skipping those stages. One potential solutions is to have a `NoOpTask` which does nothing, or we could remove the requirement to define the `setup_cls` and `teardown_cls` attributes.

- In the example, the `Task` instance's "run mode" methods return their outputs, and these outputs are passed along to the next `Task`. Should we instead be setting some result attribute and using that? I did try this, but found myself forgetting to set the attribute when writing up the example. It feels more familiar returning the value.

## Interface Changes

No interface changes yet, but once we've got some feedback on the solver API, we can start updating the existing solvers.
