title: Proposal: `debug_naughty_geometry` decorator
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

I'm always frustrated when a geometry operation fails with a `FreeCADError` and sometimes it can be a pain to recreate that geometry in order to understand better why the operation failed.

I thought it would be nice to have a decorator that stashes the failed operation in such a way that it is possible to inspect the state of affairs after the fact. I think it's likely we're going to get a lot of issues raised on geometry operations as they can be temperamental. So it would be nice to facilitate bug-reporting and debugging.

## Proposed solution

I've just used the following because I needed a failing offset in order to write a test, and it looks like it could be made into a useful decorator for some badly behaved geometry operations.

```python
    try:
        return BluemiraWire(
            cadapi.offset_wire(wire._shape, thickness, join, open_wire), label=label
        )
    except Exception as e:
        import json
        import os
        from bluemira.base.file import get_bluemira_path
        from datetime import datetime
        wire_dict = serialize_shape(wire)
        fp = get_bluemira_path("naughty_geometry", subfolder="generated_data")
        name = "offset_wire"+str(datetime.now())
        fn = os.sep.join([fp, name])

        with open(fn, "w") as file:
            json.dump(wire_dict, file, indent=4)
        raise e
```
Obviously, you'd want to capture the input arguments in the JSON as well.

Thoughts @ivanmaione @je-cook @hsaunders1904 ?

title: Bump pyparsing from 3.0.7 to 3.0.8
body:
Bumps [pyparsing](https://github.com/pyparsing/pyparsing) from 3.0.7 to 3.0.8.
Release notes

Sourced from pyparsing's releases.

pyparsing 3.0.8

Version 3.0.8 -

  • API CHANGE: modified pyproject.toml to require Python version 3.6.8 or later for pyparsing 3.x. Earlier minor versions of 3.6 fail in evaluating the version_info class (implemented using typing.NamedTuple). If you are using an earlier version of Python 3.6, you will need to use pyparsing 2.4.7.

  • Improved pyparsing import time by deferring regex pattern compiles. PR submitted by Anthony Sottile to fix issue #362, thanks!

  • Updated build to use flit, PR by Michał Górny, added BUILDING.md doc and removed old Windows build scripts - nice cleanup work!

  • More type-hinting added for all arithmetic and logical operator methods in ParserElement. PR from Kazantcev Andrey, thank you.

  • Fixed infix_notation's definitions of lpar and rpar, to accept parse expressions such that they do not get suppressed in the parsed results. PR submitted by Philippe Prados, nice work.

  • Fixed bug in railroad diagramming with expressions containing Combine elements. Reported by Jeremy White, thanks!

  • Added show_groups argument to create_diagram to highlight grouped elements with an unlabeled bounding box.

  • Added unicode_denormalizer.py to the examples as a demonstration of how Python's interpreter will accept Unicode characters in identifiers, but normalizes them back to ASCII so that identifiers print and 𝕡𝓻ᵢ𝓃𝘁 and 𝖕𝒓𝗂𝑛ᵗ are all equivalent.

  • Removed imports of deprecated sre_constants module for catching exceptions when compiling regular expressions. PR submitted by Serhiy Storchaka, thank you.

  • Fix casting error when using to_reduced_units with array of int. (Issue #1184)

title: Components can have the same name at the same depth in a tree
body:
## Describe the bug

Components with the same name can have the same depth within a tree. The following tree is possible:

```txt
TFCoils (Component)
├── Sector 1 (Component)
└── Sector 1 (Component)
```

Seeing as we access components by name (via `get_component`), it feels as though we shouldn't have more than one component with the same name at the same level.

## Steps to reproduce

There are two ways to recreate the behaviour:

```python 
parent = Component("TFCoils")
Component("Sector 1", parent=parent)
Component("Sector 1", parent=parent)
print(parent.tree())
```

```python
parent = Component("TFCoils")
parent.add_child(Component("Sector 1"))
parent.add_child(Component("Sector 1"))
print(parent.tree())
```

## Expected behaviour

We should raise an error in this case.

```python
    def test_add_child_ComponentError_given_duplicated_component_name(self):
        parent = Component("TFCoils")
        parent.add_child(Component("Sector 1"))

        with pytest.raises(ComponentError):
            parent.add_child(Component("Sector 1"))

    def test_init_ComponentError_given_duplicated_component_name(self):
        parent = Component("TFCoils")
        Component("Sector 1", parent=parent)

        with pytest.raises(ComponentError):
            Component("Sector 1", parent=parent)
````

title: Add TF coil inter-structure supports to EU-DEMO
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We need to add a simple design optimisation problem for the additional inter-coil structures for the TF coils and add Components to the reactor tree.

## Proposed solution

In BLUEPRINT, the OIS were optimised for EU-DEMO by maximising straight length along a segment of TF coil in between ports, with the constraint that the rectangle should sit fully within the x-z cross-section of the TF casing.

In a first pass, I imagine we could do the same here.

## Alternative solutions

Manufacturing concerns have been raised in the past w.r.t. curved OIS.

## Additional context

These would eventually be used in the beam finite element model of the TF coil cage.

title: Add pulsed PF coil current optimisation for fixed coilset design
body:
## Linked Issues

This is a first pass refactor of the PF coilset optimisation problems. I've decided to stop here to keep the size of the PR down. There are probably a few spin-off PRs that can take place after this to address some useful refactors, such as:

* The dissolution of the `eq.force_field` attribute in favour of building the response matrices for coilset field and force constraints outside of `ForceField` and certainly outside of `Equilibrium`
* The refactor of equilibrium constraints to subclass directly from `OptimisationConstraint` and build their response matrices upon instantiation (and rebuild as required upon update) rather than passing the response matrices into the args of the constraint function (which is then wrapped by the user in an `OptimisationConstraint`. see #1027 
* Address the API of `eq_constraints` and `opt_constraints` in `equilibria`; they are very similar philosophically, and should probably all be `opt_constraints`. For example, the user should be able to choose between lumping a field null constraint into an L2 norm of a set of magnetic targets, or using a field null constraint directly in an optimisation problem. see #1027
* Refactor iterators see #1027
* Add a new converger for equilibria after the iterators are refactored.


I really struggled to get all of the functionality that is in this PR into a configurable design problem. There are so many layers of different objects that could be specified in different combinations. To access this all via a configurable `build_config` for {"PF Coils": {"runmode": run, "build_config": {...}} seems like the way to go, but I couldn't find a neat way of doing it and it was slowing me down. I thought it best to get something working first, then perhaps @hsaunders1904  or @je-cook could help out with plugging it all back in so that it is configurable from the `Reactor`'s `build_config`?

## Description

Adds the skeleton of a new `run.py` interface to `equilibria`.

I've flipped the objective of the optimisation problem to being the minimisation of the squared currents, with a constraint on the L2 norm of the magnetic targets, which I believe is what CREATE does. This is still debatable, and it's hard to determine a value of the rms of the L2 norm below which a plasma is "acceptable". This is in particular because we don't constrain "gaps" but rather an isoflux, and at the moment the field null is lumped in the L2-norm of the magnetic targets, meaning that the value of the constraint is in mixed units. Some of the TODOs listed above could help solve this problem.

title: Refactor PictureFrame parameterisation
body:
## Description

This creates a factory metaclass for picture frame and removes all extra pictureframe classes while keeping the same functionality. 

I have quite extensively used lambda functions assigned to variables which flake doesnt like but I couldnt think of a cleaner way to organise the code and loads of 1 lines functions seemed overkill. Better suggestions welcomed.

I still want to add a few more tests (for failure modes) but it is ready for a general structure review

@shaildesai96 you may be interested

## Interface Changes

For complex pictureframe structures you now specify the leg type when setting up the class eg full domed looks like

```python
PictureFrame(upper="CURVED", lower="CURVED")
```

- [x] Tests run locally and pass `pytest tests --reactor`

Bumps [wrapt](https://github.com/GrahamDumpleton/wrapt) from 1.14.0 to 1.14.1.
Changelog

Sourced from wrapt's changelog.

Version 1.14.1

Bugs Fixed

  • When the post import hooks mechanism was being used, and a Python package with its own custom module importer was used, importing modules could fail if the custom module importer didn't use the latest Python import hook finder/loader APIs and instead used the deprecated API. This was actually occurring with the zipimporter in Python itself, which was not updated to use the newer Python APIs until Python 3.10.

body:
Bumps [shapely](https://github.com/shapely/shapely) from 1.8.1.post1 to 1.8.2.
Release notes

Sourced from shapely's releases.

1.8.2

Version 1.8.2 fixes 3 bugs, one of them a significant memory leak in shapely.ops.nearest_points. We have more built distributions in https://pypi.org/project/Shapely/1.8.2/#files than ever before. In a nutshell, Pythons 3.6-3.10 for older platforms, and Pythons 3.8-3.10 for newer platforms including arm64 linux. Only Pythons 3.9 and 3.10 are supported on arm64 macos. All these built distributions include GEOS 3.10.2.

title: Bump matplotlib from 3.5.1 to 3.5.2
body:
Bumps [matplotlib](https://github.com/matplotlib/matplotlib) from 3.5.1 to 3.5.2.
Release notes

Sourced from matplotlib's releases.

REL: v3.5.2

This is the second bugfix release of the 3.5.x series.

This release contains several bug-fixes and adjustments:

  • Add support for Windows on ARM (source-only; no wheels provided yet)
  • Add year to concise date formatter when displaying less than 12 months
  • Disable QuadMesh mouse cursor to avoid severe performance regression in pcolormesh
  • Delay backend selection to allow choosing one in more cases
  • Fix automatic layout bugs in EPS output
  • Fix autoscaling of scatter plots
  • Fix clearing of subfigures
  • Fix colorbar exponents, inversion of extensions, and use on inset axes
  • Fix compatibility with various NumPy-like classes (e.g., Pandas, xarray, etc.)
  • Fix constrained layout bugs with mixed subgrids
  • Fix errorbar with dashes
  • Fix errors in conversion to GTK4 and Qt6
  • Fix figure options accidentally re-ordering data
  • Fix keyboard focus of TkAgg backend
  • Fix manual selection of contour labels
  • Fix path effects on text with whitespace
  • Fix quiver in subfigures
  • Fix RangeSlider.set_val displaying incorrectly
  • Fix regressions in collection data limits
  • Fix stairs with no edgecolor
  • Fix some leaks in Tk backends
  • Fix tight layout DPI confusion
  • Fix tool button customizability and some tool manager bugs
  • Only set Tk HiDPI scaling-on-map for Windows systems
  • Partially allow TTC font collection files by selecting the first font

body:
## Describe the bug

The tests in `tests/display/test_plotter.py` fail with an `AttributeError`:
```log
E       AttributeError: module 'bluemira.geometry' has no attribute 'tools'
```

However, the tests do not fail if you run all the tests in the `display` directory, i.e., running the following the tests will pass.

```console
pytest tests/display/
```
Hence, this is not showing up in the CI.

I suspect some strange import shenanigans going on here.

## Steps to reproduce

```console
pytest tests/display/test_plotter.py
```

## Expected behaviour

Tests pass when only that test file is run.

title: ✨ Polyscope CAD viewer
body:
UPDATE AS OF 3/01/23

This has been updated as a separate backed of which there are now 2. 
I am getting asked more often for 'pretty' CAD ie renderings which polyscope can provide.

Side benefit we are now completely disconnected from the view irrelevant of backend. It is all dynamic.

let me know any thoughts, personally I think its worth the minor maintenance load, and the default is still freecad

## Linked Issues

Closes #1859

## Description

This PR replaces the old CAD viewer with one made with polyscope ([polyscope.run](https://polyscope.run)) which is easily installed with `pip install polyscope` all its dependencies seem to be built into the binary removing many chances for crashes/errors especially prevalent in graphical things.

Upsides:
- Quick (full reactor view ~10s)
- Pretty (materials eg wax, candy give good looking/metallic effects)
- Configurable before and during viewing (you can slice on the fly)
- antialiasing can be enable to improve quality 
- screenshot button built in
- No longer tied to freecad's viewer
- Programmable flying around object within callbacks possible
- Custom UI elements can be developed

Downsides:
- All objects have to be tessellated into a mesh to be viewed (the reason for not being faster)


~Current implementation specific (fixable with some work):~
  ~Wires in the current implementation cannot be viewed because my naiive implementation only works the the object has a face~
    ~Objects with wires without faces attached but still with some faces will only show the faces not the wires~
    ~The following two tests will fail with `--plotting-on` until this is fixed:~
        ~`tests/display/test_displayer.py::TestComponentDisplayer::test_display`~
        ~`tests/display/test_displayer.py::TestGeometryDisplayer::test_display`~ Wires now work
- We no longer have infinite inertia :smiling_face_with_tear: 

Thanks to @smason for doing the initial legwork!

## Interface Changes

A few new optional options for both viewing objects and changing the behaviour of the viewer

- [X] Code quality checks run locally and pass `flake8` and `black .`

title: `BetaIpLiProfile` based on a flux function parameterisation and plasma integral matching
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

With the refactor of the iterators #1027, we'll be losing some functionality; namely the ability to constrain the plasma profile `l_i` integral during iteration. I'm not sure yet if this actually helps convergence, to be honest, and it may be that we need to re-instate this functionality down the line.

With `BetaIpProfile` one can constrain `beta_p` but not `l_i` simultaneously.

We should however have the functionality to let the user determine their own flux functions based on matching the desired plasma integral values (`beta_p` and `l_i`) for a given plasma shape and profile parameterisation. 

## Proposed solution

Add `BetaIpLiProfile` which provides flux function optimisation preserving `beta_p` `l_i` and `I_p`.

## Alternative solutions

We're mostly moving towards using `CustomProfile` with pre-ascertained flux functions when solving equilibria nowadays. We sacrifice consistency on plasma integrals slightly, but provided the flux functions come from a transport solver of some kind, it is generally felt this is acceptable. The integrals `beta_p` and `l_i` are effectively results. This is fine, but requires a user to have flux functions that provide the desired integrals. As these flux functions in any case tend to come from transport solvers with a fixed boundary and no X-point(s) the integrals will only ever be approximate.

title: Refactor EUDEMOReactor's build_cryo_thermal_shield method
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

After #980, there is some inconsistency in the `design_stage` methods of the reactor. Most design stages return the components that they've built, which are then added to the component tree in the `run` method. However, `build_cryo_thermal_shield` is not doing this. It does not return the component it builds, but adds it to the component tree itself.

We should make `build_cryo_thermal_shield` more consistent with the other design stages, and only add components to the reactor tree within the `run` method.

Relevant [PR comment here](https://github.com/Fusion-Power-Plant-Framework/bluemira/pull/980#discussion_r864555471).

## Proposed solution

Make the `THERMAL_SHIELD` component in the `run` method, add that to the component tree. Then call the `build_VV_thermal_shield` and `build_cryo_thermal_shield` design stages, but add their return values to the `THERMAL_SHIELD` component.

Note that we can't build both the VVTS and CTS together, as the coil builders depend on the VVTS, and the CTS depends on the coils.

```python
def run(self) -> Component:
    ...
    thermal_shield = Component(self.THERMAL_SHIELD)
    component.add_child(thermal_shield)
    ...
    thermal_shield.add_child(self.build_VV_thermal_shield())
    ...
    thermal_shield.add_child(self.build_cryo_thermal_shield())
```

Relevant [PR comment here](https://github.com/Fusion-Power-Plant-Framework/bluemira/pull/980#discussion_r870022101).

title: Improve design/documentation of slice_shape
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

I'm a little confused about the API of [`bluemira.geometry.tools.slice_shape`](https://github.com/Fusion-Power-Plant-Framework/bluemira/blob/07e6d83705597a15410705a158d87e9c2ada5e2d/bluemira/geometry/tools.py#L774).

The docstring suggests that the function returns a tuple, but I think what it means is, _if the input is a wire it returns x, if the input is one of these other geoms, then return y_. I'm not really sure.

Also, we may wish to consider the name, the function isn't actually _slicing_ anything. It's finding the intersections between a shape and a plane. 

## Proposed solution

I'm not a big fan of functions returning multiple types. It puts a lot of burden on the caller to check their outputs after the call. I propose to split the function up into separate functions, where each one only returns a single type. So we may end up with something like:

```python
def split_wire(wire: BluemiraWire, plane: BluemiraPlane) -> np.ndarray:
    ...

def split_face(face: BluemiraFace, plane: BluemiraPlane) -> BluemiraWire:
   ...

def split_shape_3d(shape: Union[BluemiraSolid, BluemiraShell], plane: BluemiraPlane) -> List[BluemiraWire]:
   ...
```

If the plane does not intercept the shape, we could potentially return `None` (make the return type `Optional`), but I would tend to prefer raising an error; EAFP over LBYL.

## Alternative solutions

We stick with the current `slice_shape` but we document more clearly what the inputs/outputs are. This still shifts the burden to the caller to check their inputs/outputs when using the function, which, in a public API, I would find not great.

title: `ParameterFrame`, `Configuration` and the setup of individual `Builder` `Solver` etc.
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

At present all `Parameter`s are "hosted" with default values in a `Configuration` object. Many of these `Parameter`s are used in several locations in every run, regardless of what `Reactor` is being designed. This is partly because of interfaces to codes like `PROCESS` and `PLASMOD` which require a full set of inputs.

Many of these `Parameter`s can be considered as "globals" in the context of a reactor design, even if some of them are recalculated in subsequent steps or may even deviate at different snapshots in time from the reference values.

However, many more `Parameter`s are specific to a certain build stage, `Builder`, or `Solver`. In some cases, these `Parameter`s are not used if an alternative `Builder` or `Solver` is used for a given build stage. This leaves the "global" `Configuration` pre-populated with `Parameter`s that have no relevance for a given design.

## Proposed solution

Reduce the `Parameter`s hosted in `Configuration` to the "global" `Parameter`s and enable `Builder`s and `Solver`s to be initialised both from the global `Configuration` and from a local `ParameterFrame` or `Configuration`.

This may complicate the initialisation somewhat, but will provide a clearer picture of what `Parameter`s are used where.

title: `BluemiraGeo` should explicitly be "static" and not "dynamic"
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

At present, it is possible to update e.g. a `BluemiraWire` that could have propagating effects on other `BluemiraGeo`s built from that wire.

We have discussed the possibility of making use of this type of "dynamic" functionality, but given that the "update" of the reactor for a changed geometry is not a standard procedure, and would require a form of callback procedure which is likely to be different in each case, we have decided not to do this. Whilst this would be desirable, the cost of implementing and managing the callbacks for any possible geometry modification is considered to be too high for our resources.

## Proposed solution

Explicitly state that `BluemiraGeo` is "static" in the documentation.

Protect against propagating effects by liberal use of `deepcopy`.

## Alternative solutions
See above

## Additional context

Even with adequate resources, this is not a development priority at the moment (we are still working on the "single-pass" build chain).


@ivanmaione  as discussed.

title: Some closure inconsistencies may be causing bugs or cause bugs in future.
body:
## Describe the bug

When a wire is closed in the primitive form, I assume this means that its start and end points are coincident to within some tolerance. I do not know if FreeCAD automatically "snaps" them to be mathematically identical, but I suspect not.

I've noticed that when discretising a closed wire with `byedges=False` the resulting numpy array (under the hood) is not closed in such a way that when passed into `Coordinates` it is considered open (i.e. that `np.allclose(points[0], points[-1], rtol=0, atol=EPS) == False`

If I pass this "open" set of `Coordinates` back into `make_polygon`, the resulting wire is indeed closed (even with `make_polygon(coordinates, closed=False)`.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

```python
from bluemira.geometry.parameterisations import TripleArc
from bluemira.builders.EUDEMO.tools import varied_offset

wire = TripleArc().create_shape()
coordinates = wire.discretize(ndiscr=100, byedges=False)

offset_wire = varied_offset(wire, 0.2, 0.6, 60, 160, num_points=200)

print(offset_wire.is_closed())

offset_coordinates = offset_wire.discretize(ndiscr=100, byedges=False)
print(offset_coordinates.closed)
```

## Expected behaviour

I expect the discretisation of closed wire to be closed within machine precision. Alternatively I expect that our "machine precision for geometry" be the same across FreeCAD and discretised representations.

## Additional context
I'm investigating the various issues we are seeing in the EU-DEMO build where occasionally we get open wires, disjointed faces, reconstruction errors, etc. I'm not sure that this is related, but I'm trying to bomb-proof stuff as much as possible!

@ivanmaione FYI

title: Add a `GEOMETRY_TOLERANCE` or similar and use for treatment of geometry
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

FreeCAD's tolerance is of 1e-7 and we often use EPS in geometry in bluemira, which is much smaller than this and designed really for machine precision.

## Proposed solution

We should use a tolerance for geometry more consistent with that of FreeCAD. This has come in the context of checking for closed wires and coordinates, but is likely to be relevant elsewhere too.

title: Inconsistencies in `geometry/tools.py` and `_freecadapi.py`
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

There are few places in `_freecadapi.py` where we are doing things above and beyond what FreeCAD is doing, such that it is more than just a "pure" interface. There are also some functions that are used directly in e.g. `BluemiraWire` that do not have corresponding functions in `geometry/tools.py`

## Proposed solution

We should discuss the strategy in the geometry workshop in KIT, and then implement a consistent approach, whatever that may be.

title: Dependency management changes and release procedure
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

As we start becoming more stable we should have a release cycle and adjust how we deal with dependencies.


## Proposed solution

A release (not necessarily a full release eg 0.0.0a1) will happen every 6 weeks, immediately after which the new dependencies updates will be merged into develop.
Dependency updates should be tracked in a separate a branch `develop_dependencies` that tracks develop. These new dependencies will run on the CI so that breakages are caught and fixed early. New dependencies should be merged in to develop every ~6 weeks creating a more stable environment for new features to be added.

First step is in #1068 separate out dependencies into their minimal areas the full list to first tag:

The docker containers are just awaiting our conversion to dolfinx

Live with unstableness and never release

We need a nice workflow in order for everyone to be able to improve the code while not being disrupted too often

title: Bump coverage[toml] from 6.3.3 to 6.4
body:
Bumps [coverage[toml]](https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy) from 6.3.3 to 6.4.
Release notes

Sourced from coverage[toml]'s releases.

6.4

  • A new setting, [run] sigterm, controls whether a SIGTERM signal handler is used. In 6.3, the signal handler was always installed, to capture data at unusual process ends. Unfortunately, this introduced other problems (see issue 1310). Now the signal handler is only used if you opt-in by setting [run] sigterm = true.
  • Small changes to the HTML report:
    • Added links to next and previous file, and more keyboard shortcuts: [ and ] for next file and previous file; u for up to the index; and ? to open/close the help panel. Thanks, J. M. F. Tsang.
    • The timestamp and version are displayed at the top of the report. Thanks, Ammar Askar. Closes issue 1351.
  • A new debug option debug=sqldata adds more detail to debug=sql, logging all the data being written to the database.
  • Previously, running coverage report (or any of the reporting commands) in an empty directory would create a .coverage data file. Now they do not, fixing issue 1328.
  • On Python 3.11, the [toml] extra no longer installs tomli, instead using tomllib from the standard library. Thanks Shantanu.
  • In-memory CoverageData objects now properly update(), closing issue 1323.
Changelog

Sourced from coverage[toml]'s changelog.

Version 6.4 — 2022-05-22

  • A new setting, :ref:config_run_sigterm, controls whether a SIGTERM signal handler is used. In 6.3, the signal handler was always installed, to capture data at unusual process ends. Unfortunately, this introduced other problems (see issue 1310_). Now the signal handler is only used if you opt-in by setting [run] sigterm = true.

  • Small changes to the HTML report:

    • Added links to next and previous file, and more keyboard shortcuts: [ and ] for next file and previous file; u for up to the index; and ? to open/close the help panel. Thanks, J. M. F. Tsang <pull 1364_>_.

    • The timestamp and version are displayed at the top of the report. Thanks, Ammar Askar <pull 1354_>. Closes issue 1351.

  • A new debug option debug=sqldata adds more detail to debug=sql, logging all the data being written to the database.

  • Previously, running coverage report (or any of the reporting commands) in an empty directory would create a .coverage data file. Now they do not, fixing issue 1328_.

  • On Python 3.11, the [toml] extra no longer installs tomli, instead using tomllib from the standard library. Thanks Shantanu <pull 1359_>_.

  • In-memory CoverageData objects now properly update(), closing issue 1323_.

title: Numpy deprecation warning in BalanceOfPlant
body:
## Describe the bug

Running the `steady_state_example.py` script causes a depreciation warning.

## Steps to reproduce

Run the `examples/balance_of_plant/steady_state_example.py` script.

```console
> python examples/balance_of_plant/steady_state_example.py 
VisibleDeprecationWarning: Creating an ndarray from ragged nested sequences (which is a list-or-tuple of lists-or-tuples-or ndarrays with different lengths or shapes) is deprecated. If you meant to do this, you must specify 'dtype=object' when creating the ndarray.
  return ufunc.reduce(obj, axis, dtype, out, **passkwargs)
```

## Expected behaviour

No deprecation warning.

The warning originates from [this line](https://github.com/Fusion-Power-Plant-Framework/bluemira/blob/99f556bd65580b15a338fc4b84397122913b08e1/bluemira/balance_of_plant/steady_state.py#L538) in `BalanceOfPlant.sanity`, and is caused by the summing of a list of lists of various sizes using numpy (which I assume is converting to an array, which causes the warning).

A potential solution is to not use numpy to sum the lists.

We're actually already summing all the individual sub-lists as a sanity check, so it's a bit wasteful to sum then again anyway.

## Environment

The `numpy` version in my environment is 1.21.5.

title: Add actions for release workflow
body:
## Linked Issues

Partially addresses #1087 

## Description

This PR adds GitHub Actions workflows to produce releases of bluemira.

Please have a read through of the accompanying documentation to familiarise yourself with the process/suggest improvements.

### Release Notes

There is still the question of release notes. At the moment, these are auto-generated by the GitHub CLI, which basically lists out, and links to, pull requests that have been merged since the last release. This requires no extra work from us, but doesn't really offer users any indication to which changes are important to them.

Another option is [`towncrier'](https://github.com/twisted/towncrier). This will generate release notes for us, from small snippets that we push with every pull request. We create a file for each pull request, where we let it know what kind of pull request it is (a new feature, bugfix, documentation, etc.), an associated issue number, and write a small (often one line) comment on what's been added. When we need it to, it will build the snippets into a release notes document, and remove the snippets for that release. 

`towncrier` also has a `check` command, which we can run on the CI to remind us to add a release notes snippet.

Let me know what you think.

## Checklist

I confirm that I have completed the following checks:

- [ ] Tests run locally and pass `pytest tests --reactor`
- [ ] Code quality checks run locally and pass `flake8` and `black .`
- [x] Documentation built locally and checked `sphinx-build -W documentation/source documentation/build`

Release notes

Sourced from requests's releases.

v2.28.0

2.28.0 (2022-06-09)

Deprecations

  • ⚠️ Requests has officially dropped support for Python 2.7. ⚠️ (#6091)
  • Requests has officially dropped support for Python 3.6 (including pypy3). (#6091)

Improvements

  • Wrap JSON parsing issues in Request's JSONDecodeError for payloads without an encoding to make json() API consistent. (#6097)
  • Parse header components consistently, raising an InvalidHeader error in all invalid cases. (#6154)
  • Added provisional 3.11 support with current beta build. (#6155)
  • Requests got a makeover and we decided to paint it black. (#6095)

  • Fixed issue where invalid Windows registry entires caused proxy resolution to raise an exception rather than ignoring the entry. (#6149)

title: Separation of concerns - `Builder` / `OptimisationProblem` / `["run", "read", "mock"]`
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We have a couple of situations in the EU-DEMO reactor where we are solving a design optimisation problem in an `OptimisationProblem` and subsequently building some geometry in a dedicated `Builder`. This is the case for at least:
* TF coils
* PF coils (see #1113)

At present, the `Builder` handles the `["run", "read", "mock"]` logic and in the case of `"run"` actually runs the design optimisation problem. This means that a lot of parameters that are technically only required for the `"run"` case are passed into the `Builder`.

It is also relatively opaque in terms of separation of concerns: in many people's heads a `Builder` is responsible for creating geometry, regardless of what inputs it has been given.

The most complicated situation is that of the TF coils, where the aspects of the builder are directly used in the optimisation problem being solved in the case of run. As such this is perhaps the best testing ground for an alternative solution.

## Proposed solution

Make `Builder`s solely responsible for generating CAD.

Split out the concern of `["run", "read", "mock"]` from the `Builder` , potentially instead being managed by the `design_stage` itself(?).

If necessary, the optimisation problem may have to call the `Builder`, but this would be quite "circular" and should be avoided if possible. in the case of the PF coils, for instance, this should not be necessary at all.

## Alternative solutions

There are many ways of slicing this one. To be discussed in the architecture workshop.

title: `Equilibrium` `PlasmaCoil` speed and logic improvements
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

When optimising PF coil positions we tend to "freeze" the plasma contributions which is presently done via a `PlasmaCoil` object that behaves like a `Coil` with a fixed current (albeit with a variable current density).

This is quite slow to instantiate, and what's more is quite slow to call (or rather slower than it could be).

## Proposed solution

Cache plasma coil (coming in anyway with #1113) but also for points on the grid make use of psi, Bx, and Bz interpolation rather than convolving Greens' functions. For points off the grid, convolve greens functions (if at all necessary) with stashed response matrices.

title: Homogeneous coilset opt problem constraints name
body:
## Requirement to address

The equilibrium coilset optimization problem classes uses a different name for the `[OptimizationConstraint]` inputs between the differnent classes:
- `opt_constraints` for `NestedCoilsetPositionCOP` and `CoilsetPositionCOP`
- `constraints` for `TikhonovCurrentCOP` and the other new optimization problems

To setup a optimization set input agnostic to any optimization problem (so we can set the optimiztion in a `.json` input file) without having to write too much `if` statements, it would be easier to make the COP inputs names the same.

With that we could have some nice functionnal programming such as 

``` python

def set_optimiser(optimiser_options=None):
    if optimiser_options is not None:
        optimiser = Optimiser(**optimiser_options)
    else:
        optimiser = None
    return optimiser


def get_coilset_op_cls(coilset_op_cls):
    allowed_coilset_ops = {
        "UnconstrainedTikhonovCurrentGradientCOP": UnconstrainedTikhonovCurrentGradientCOP,
        "TikhonovCurrentCOP": TikhonovCurrentCOP,
        "CoilsetPositionCOP": CoilsetPositionCOP,
        "NestedCoilsetPositionCOP": NestedCoilsetPositionCOP,
    }
    return allowed_coilset_ops[coilset_op_cls]


def set_coilset_opt_problem(
    coilset,
    coilset_op_cls_name,
    eq,
    targets,
    eq_config,
    opt_constraints=None,
):
    """
    Instantiate the PF coil optimization problem
    
    NOTE: currently full of if statement and not using structured inputs.
    This is mean to be resolved in separated merge requests.    
    """
    # Coilset optimization problem (COP) input dict
    # - #
    # Json input specified input
    coilset_cop_input = eq_config["fbe_optimization_options"]

    # Common inputs
    coilset_cop_input["coilset"] = coilset
    coilset_cop_input["eq"] = eq
    coilset_cop_input["targets"] = targets

    # NLopt optimization inputs (Optimizer)
    if coilset_op_cls_name not in ["UnconstrainedTikhonovCurrentGradientCOP"]:
        coilset_cop_input["optimiser"] = set_optimiser(eq_config["optimiser"])

        # Optimization constraints
        coilset_cop_input["opt_constraints"] = opt_constraints
    #  
    # - #
    
    # Declaring the opt class object
    coilset_cop_cls = get_coilset_op_cls(coilset_op_cls_name)

    return coilset_cop_cls(**coilset_cop_input)
```

Otherwise I will have to make a class dependent set of the optimization constraints

title: Run plotting tests with non-interactive backend
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

We currently have a suite of plotting tests, however these are not run in the CI, so it's always too late before we see that they're broken. It's also not easy for runners of the tests to immediately see if something is wrong, unless they are very familiar with what the figures should look like. 

We want to run these tests in the CI to ensure the tests at least run without error. In an ideal world, we would also programmatically make some assertions about the resulting figures. Typically, we might save a reference figure and compare it to the figure produced by the test using [`matplotlib.testing.compare`](https://matplotlib.org/stable/api/testing_api.html#module-matplotlib.testing.compare). You can also test attributes of the figure, Matplotlib exposes `Artist` objects (lines, patches, etc.) on `Axes`, that we can check attributes of (e.g., coordinates, colo[u]r).

## Proposed solution

We turn off Matplotlib's interactive backend when running the tests without `--plotting-on`; i.e., `--plotting-on` turns on the interactive backend. This way the plot objects will be created, but will not open blocking displays.

The above will work for many of our tests, but we also need to consider the CAD viewer. I'm open to ideas on how we can stop that blocking the running of the tests. A quick and dirty solution is to just mock it out everywhere.

## Outputs

- The ability to run the plotting tests without GUIs blocking the execution of the test suite.
- The plotting tests run on the CI.

title: Add warnings and run more tests for the develop_dependencies merge PR
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

It would be nice to both run the longrun tests and print any warnings in a comment when merging in `develop_dependencies` so we don't missing warnings in the CI

## Proposed solution

Add `pytest-json-report` to our pytest plugins and run:

`pytest --json-report --json-report-indent=3 --reactor --longrun --private`

the following couple of commands will filter the warnings and print the number we have from the generated report:
`jq '.warnings | length' .report.json`
`jq '.warnings | unique' .report.json`

There is possibly a nice way to format that in a comment but code quotes would also be fine.

I think it would be possible to just modify our existing `ci.yml` eg naiively with an extra environment variable:
```
env:
     PYEST_LONGRUN: ${{ github.ref_name == "develop_dependencies" && "--longrun" || "" }}
```

## Alternative solutions

Just add the `--longrun` tests for the dependencies PR

title: Bump numpy from 1.22.4 to 1.23.0
body:
Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 1.22.4 to 1.23.0.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v1.23.0

NumPy 1.23.0 Release Notes

The NumPy 1.23.0 release continues the ongoing work to improve the handling and promotion of dtypes, increase the execution speed, clarify the documentation, and expire old deprecations. The highlights are:

  • Implementation of loadtxt in C, greatly improving its performance.
  • Exposing DLPack at the Python level for easy data exchange.
  • Changes to the promotion and comparisons of structured dtypes.
  • Improvements to f2py.

See below for the details,

New functions

  • A masked array specialization of ndenumerate is now available as numpy.ma.ndenumerate. It provides an alternative to numpy.ndenumerate and skips masked values by default.

    (gh-20020)

  • numpy.from_dlpack has been added to allow easy exchange of data using the DLPack protocol. It accepts Python objects that implement the __dlpack__ and __dlpack_device__ methods and returns a ndarray object which is generally the view of the data of the input object.

    (gh-21145)

Deprecations

  • Setting __array_finalize__ to None is deprecated. It must now be a method and may wish to call super().__array_finalize__(obj) after checking for None or if the NumPy version is sufficiently new.

    (gh-20766)

  • Using axis=32 (axis=np.MAXDIMS) in many cases had the same meaning as axis=None. This is deprecated and axis=None must be used instead.

    (gh-20920)

  • The hook function PyDataMem_SetEventHook has been deprecated and the demonstration of its use in tool/allocation_tracking has been removed. The ability to track allocations is now built-in to python via tracemalloc.

... (truncated)

title: Solver architecture for parameters and reactor design stages
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Following the two ADRs created in #1194 and #1192, we have some options for how to re-structure reactor builds and their configuration.

This issue is to investigate a new architecture for reactor builds, and to implement a `DesignStage` class that handles the `read`, `run`, `mock` logic for each stage of the reactor build.

## Proposed solution

The `DesignStage` class will need `read`, `run`, `mock` methods, which means it will be very similar to a solver. In many cases, `DesignStage`s will share similar setup (parsing and setting-up configuration), so a new class that inherits from solver, using shared setup may make sense.

## Alternative solutions

See ADRs

title: Develop initial structure for Power Cycle module
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
BLUEMIRA should boast of a power balance calculation to compute the net electricity produced by the plant. As a first approach to this issue, an initial module should be implemented to house all of the essential calculations with this aim.

## Proposed solution
For consistency, the module should be named Power Cycle (analogously to the Fuel Cycle), and should include two internal routines:
- Recirculating Power Loads, that identifies the electrical power consumed by the plant
- Balance-of-Plant, that identifies the power produced by the plant

A master manager class should retrieve the calculations of each sub-module and perform the subtraction, to compute the net power produced by the plant.
Inputs could be retrieved from a file or implemented directly in a builder class.

## Additional context
The module should incorporate some features of the old BLUEPRINT code, such as visualization through a power flow diagram.

title: Bump fonttools from 4.33.3 to 4.34.4
body:
Bumps [fonttools](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools) from 4.33.3 to 4.34.4.
Release notes

Sourced from fonttools's releases.

4.34.4

  • Fixed typo in varLib/merger.py that causes NameError merging COLR glyphs containing more than 255 layers (#2685).

4.34.3

  • [designspaceLib] Don't make up bad PS names when no STAT data (#2684)

4.34.2

  • [varStore/subset] fixed KeyError exception to do with NO_VARIATION_INDEX while subsetting varidxes in GPOS/GDEF (a08140d).

4.34.1

  • [instancer] When optimizing HVAR/VVAR VarStore, use_NO_VARIATION_INDEX=False to avoid including NO_VARIATION_INDEX in AdvWidthMap, RsbMap, LsbMap mappings, which would push the VarIdx width to maximum (4bytes), which is not desirable. This also fixes a hard crash when attempting to subset a varfont after it had been partially instanced with use_NO_VARIATION_INDEX=True.

4.34.0

  • [instancer] Set RIBBI bits in head and OS/2 table when cutting instances and the subfamily nameID=2 contains strings like 'Italic' or 'Bold' (#2673).
  • [otTraverse] Addded module containing methods for traversing trees of otData tables (#2660).
  • [otTables] Made DeltaSetIndexMap TTX dump less verbose by omitting no-op entries (#2660).
  • [colorLib.builder] Added option to disable PaintColrLayers's reuse of layers from LayerList (#2660).
  • [varLib] Added support for merging multiple master COLRv1 tables into a variable COLR table (#2660, #2328). Base color glyphs of same name in different masters must have identical paint graph structure (incl. number of layers, palette indices, number of color line stops, corresponding paint formats at each level of the graph), but can differ in the variable fields (e.g. PaintSolid.Alpha). PaintVar* tables are produced when this happens and a VarStore/DeltaSetIndexMap is added to the variable COLR table. It is possible for non-default masters to be 'sparse', i.e. omit some of the color glyphs present in the default master.
  • [feaLib] Let the Parser set nameIDs 1 through 6 that were previously reserved (#2675).
  • [varLib.varStore] Support NO_VARIATION_INDEX in optimizer and instancer.
  • [feaLib] Show all missing glyphs at once at end of parsing (#2665).
  • [varLib.iup] Rewrite force-set conditions and limit DP loopback length (#2651). For Noto Sans, IUP time drops from 23s down to 9s, with only a slight size increase in the final font. This basically turns the algorithm from O(n^3) into O(n).
  • [featureVars] Report about missing glyphs in substitution rules (#2654).
  • [mutator/instancer] Added CLI flag to --no-recalc-timestamp (#2649).
  • [SVG] Allow individual SVG documents in SVG OT table to be compressed on uncompressed, and remember that when roundtripping to/from ttx. The SVG.docList is now a list of SVGDocument namedtuple-like dataclass containing an extra compressed field, and no longer a bare 3-tuple (#2645).
  • [designspaceLib] Check for descriptor types with hasattr() to allow custom classes that don't inherit the default descriptors (#2634).
  • [subset] Enable sharing across subtables of extension lookups for harfbuzz packing (#2626). Updated how table packing falls back to fontTools from harfbuzz (#2668).
  • [subset] Updated default feature tags following current Harfbuzz (#2637).
  • [svgLib] Fixed regex for real number to support e.g. 1e-4 in addition to 1.0e-4. Support parsing negative rx, ry on arc commands (#2596, #2611).
  • [subset] Fixed subsetting SinglePosFormat2 when ValueFormat=0 (#2603).

title: Enable external codes with in and out variables to map back to a singular variable
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

`P_el_net` and `P_el_net_process` are essentially the same variable but mapped to an in and out variable for process. It would be nice if we could combine these as our `send/recv` mechanics can manage where the variable is stored. I'm pretty sure that if a variable isn't received back from a solver it is still stored on the solver.

I can see in future more codes having different variables for in and out and it would be nice to contain these 

## Proposed solution

A `send_name` mapping and `recv_name` mapping. By default they would be the same thing.

## Alternative solutions

Have two variables as is the current solution

## Additional context

There may be contexts where the out variable is not as accurate as required but that should be managed by `send/recv`

title: Develop classes to build a pulse timeline for the Power Cycle
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
The Power Cycle aims at simulating a complete reactor pulse. Classes should be created to represent a generic scenario, that can used to organize the Power Cycle simulation in different pulses, each composed of different phases.

## Proposed solution
Create 3 classes to organize :
- `PowerCyclePhase` (shortest temporal period with unified characteristics for Power Cycle simulations)
- `PowerCyclePulse` (collection of phases)
- `PowerCycleScenario` (collection of pulses)
- `ScenarioBuilder` (creates a `PowerCycleScenario` instance from a `json` input file)

## Additional context
Phases will be classified as 'steady-state' or 'transient' in a subclass (namely, `BOPPhase`), for later implementation of a time-dependent Balance-of-Plant model for the Power Cycle.

title: Develop classes to represent power loads produced/consumed in the Power Cycle
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
The main calculations performed by the Power Cycle should be done in terms of time-dependent power loads. These power loads should be constructed from simple power requirement information and expected time-dependent behavior (e.g. 'ramp' or 'step').

## Proposed solution
Development of 4 classes to build power loads to be used in the Power Cycle module:
- `LoadData` (building blocks for `PowerLoad`, validates basic inputs before building them)
- `PowerLoad` (computes a time-dependent power curve based on expected behavior -- an interpolation model)
- `PhaseLoad` (set of power loads that represent the power consumption/production during a given phase, which can be normalized in time or not)
- `PulseLoad` (set of phase loads that are shifted in time to build a power curve during a pulse)

## Additional context
Phase and Pulse specifications dependent on timeline classes (#1243).

title: Develop base classes and tools for Power Cycle module
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
Many classes in the Power Cycle module present some common characteristics that can be shared by Abstract Base Classes (ABC).
Functions developed for convenience that are used by more than one class should be stand-alone for later re-location in bluemira.

## Proposed solution
Implement a `base` script that includes ABC classes for the Power Cycle module.
Implement a `tools` script with stand-alone functions to be used as convenience tools.

title: Develop Power Cycle consumption loads
body:

The Power Cycle module should include a sub-routine to sum all power consumption contributions in the power plant, to be passed to a Power Cycle manager class.

## Proposed solution

title: Develop Power Cycle production loads
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
The Power Cycle module should include a sub-routine to compute the power loads associated with the Balance-of-Plant system of the power plant, to be passed to a Power Cycle manager class.

## Proposed solution

title: Develop a Power Cycle manager class to compute net electricity
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address
To compute net electricity, the Power Cycle module should have a high-level manager class that creates power loads based on run inputs defined by `json` files. This manager class should taken into consideration 3 types of plant loads: active (consumption) loads, reactive (consumption) loads and production loads.
The class should build a net pulse load by subtracting active load from production loads.

## Proposed solution
Create a Power Cycle Manager class.

title: Transfer Sankey-diagram methods into the Power Cycle module using Scoped Tags
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

Sankey Diagrams (SDs) represent the instantaneous power balance of a system. The `power_cycle` module should be able to display its results using a SD.

## Proposed solution

Methods that build SDs are already implemented in the `balance-of-plant` module and should be transferred into the `power_cycle` module. Compatibility with the classes already defined in `power_cycle` requires defining the structured transfer of power between systems as an additional input.

A possible implementation could be the use of Scoped Tags (_vide_ [Gitlab's scoped labels](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/labels.html#scoped-labels)) to describe a hierarchy between power loads / systems / groups.
This would allow the added benefit of describing loads as belonging to particular systems or groups and provide the user with an easy way of retrieving particular sets of power loads (_e.g._ active loads only required by Magnetic systems).

Since SDs are represented for instants in time, drawing methods would require to be applied in "snapshots" (_ i.e._ for a desired time "t") of a phase/pulse/scenario.

title: Tplobo/powercycle base
body:
# Linked Issues

Classes in the `time` file close #1243 
Classes in the `net/loads` file close #1244 
Classes in files `tools` and `base` close #1245 
Classes in the `net/importers` file mock classes to import data computed by other BLUEMIRA modules (to structure a solution for #1246 & #1247)
Classes in the `net/manager` file close #1248


---
# Description
This pool request is the first contribution for a time-dependent Power Cycle module in BLUEMIRA. It adds the necessary classes to represent time-dependent power loads in the power plant.
A simple example is included in `examples/power_cycle/simple_example` to introduce users to its functionalities.
Revision of files is advised in the order presented below.


## Tool functions & classes (`tools` file, 295 LOC)
Useful functions are divided in 3 major categories, but have not been added to custom classes to enable easier reintegration in other BLUEMIRA modules. Tool classes are a 4th category of tools, and are used for input standardization/validation. These categories are listed below:

1. Validation functions, to ensure objects of certain classes have a specific format for usage in the Power Cycle module.

2. Manipulation functions, to create, copy or modify instances of base classes, such as `list`, `str` or `dict`.

3. Plotting functions, to call or modify methods of the `matplotlib` package.

4. Classes that inherit from `dict`, to organize data in pre-determined formats.


## Base classes (`base` file, 212 LOC)
All abstract base classes for definitions in the Power Cycle module:

1. `PowerCycleABC`, almost all classes in the Power Cycle module inherit from this ABC, which defines the need of instances for a 'name' and 'label'. This should be later compared and possibly standardized with the 'name' and 'long_name' parameters in other BLUEMIRA modules. Equality checks ('__eq__') between instances of children of this class ignore name and label in the comparison. Other comparisons could be implemented in the future.

2. `PowerCycleTimeABC`, ABC class for classes defined in `time`.

3. `PowerCycleLoadABC`, ABC class for classes defined in `net/loads`.
 
5. `PowerCycleImporterABC`, ABC class for classes defined in `net/importers`.


## Time classes (`time` file, 280 LOC)
In the Power Cycle module, time is structured in three main classifications: phases, pulses and scenarios. Thus, the file `time` contains the following classes:

1. `PowerCyclePhase`, instances of which are the minimal representation of time. An instance is built with a `duration_breakdown`, a dictionary in which each item identifies a time period (keys are `str` that describe the item, values are numerical). The total phase duration is the sum of breakdown elements.

2. `PowerCyclePulse`, instances of which are the minimal time representation of a scenario. An instance is built with the `phase_set` parameter, a list of PowerCyclePhase` objects in the desired order of occurrence.

3. `PowerCycleScenario`, instances of which are the largest-scale representation of plant time. An instance is built with the `pulse_set` parameter, a list of `PowerCyclePulse` objects in the desired order of occurrence. Currently in simplified implementation; in the future a `repetition` parameter should be added to specify the number of repetitions for each pulse, so that `pulse_set` does not repeat information.

4. `ScenarioBuilder`, which reads a JSON file with inputs for building a scenario, and builds a `PowerCycleScenario` object with those inputs. This class does not require naming, so it does not inherit from `PowerCycleABC`.


## Load classes (`net/loads` file, 548 LOC)
In the Power Cycle module, creation of and operations between time-dependent power curves are performed with instances of the following classes, all of which have their own particular `plot` implementation:

1. `LoadData`,  instances of which are the minimal information necessary to represent a time-dependent power signal. Each value in a `time` list is associated with a value in a `data` list. The time-characterization may be modified by "stretching" (with `_normalize_time`) or "displacement" (with `_shift_time`). No dependence is defined for values between elements of `data`.

2. `LoadModel`,  a child of the `Enum` class. Instances of this class specify which type of interpolation, computed by the `scipy.interpolate.interp1d` method, should be applied to compute values between elements of the `data` attribute of a `LoadData` object. Instances of this class are not applied directly to `LoadData`, but instead as parameters of the `PowerLoad` class.

3. `PowerLoad`, instances of which build a simple power signal with lists of `LoadData` and `LoadModel` objects. An instance can sum the contributions of each `LoadData` by interpolating values using its respective `LoadModel` specification, and can plot the total curve in time. Instances can be added to one another, and multiplied/divided by scalar values.

4. `PhaseLoad`, instances of which specify in which time period a load should occur, built with lists of `PowerLoad` and `bool` objects. The boolean list acts as a series of "normalization" flags and a `PowerCyclePhase` object passed as parameter is used to specify the total load duration; `True` flags indicate that the total time length of a `PowerLoad` should be "stretched/compressed" to fit the phase duration. Instances can be added to one another, only if representing the same phase.

6. `PulseLoad`, instances of which build the total load during a pulse using, using a list of `PhaseLoad` objects. This list acts as a library of loads for each phase of a `PowerCyclePulse` object parameter. Multiple `PhaseLoad` objects for the same phase are added. Each of these loads is displaced in time, in order to occur after the end of the last phase. Plotting includes delimiter lines at the time that each phase ends.

7. `ScenarioLoad`, instances of which build the total load during a scenario. Currently not implemented.


## Importer classes (`net/importer` file, 65 LOC)
Static classes used to represent the future implementation of data transfer from other BLUEMIRA modules into the Power Cycle module. These classes does not require naming, so they do not inherit from `PowerCycleABC`.

1. `EquilibriaImporter`, static class that will import data from the `equilibria` module. 

2. `PumpingImporter`, static class that will import data from the module that will compute "tokamak pumping" data.


## Manager classes (`net/manager` file, 320 LOC)
Classes used to build a time evolution of the power load produced and consumed in the power plant, using data from other modules and a series of input files.

1. `PowerCycleSystem`, instances of which build `PhaseLoad` objects to represent active and reactive power being produced/consumed by the power plant.

2. `PowerCycleGroup`, instances of which are used to group plant systems according to their systemic classification.

3. `PowerCycleManager`, which calls `ScenarioBuilder` and reads a JSON file with inputs for all the power loads associated with that scenario. It builds Power Cycle groups and systems, and merges their PhaseLoads in one `PulseLoad` per load type (one for "active", one for "reactive"). This class does not require naming, so it does not inherit from `PowerCycleABC`.


---
# Interface Changes
None.

title: Replace scipy's `minimize` in equilibria/fixed_boundary/utilities::`calculate_plasma_shape_params` with a more robust solution
body:
## Description of issue / requirement to address

In order to find plasma extrema in the FEM fixed boundary solution, an optimisation approach is used. At present this uses scipy's `minimize` function, which is not a particularly robust solution and does not follow the standard in the rest of the code base.

This was a "prototype" solution to the problem, for which scipy is a useful too.

## Proposed solution
Replace the scipy optimisations in the FEM fixed boundary equilibrium module with `Optimisers` and add anaytical Jacobians (for robustness). 

Interestingly, this is not a speed issue, as we are only searching for 4 points and get a reasonably good starting guess from the mesh, so no need to implement a custom CG approach.

## Alternative solutions

Leave things as are, but the interface will likely change anyway when we move away from scipy 1.5.3. We've had a whole host of issues in the past with upgrading scipy due to API changes and a lot of stuff in scipy.optimize seemed to just behave differently (IIRC).

title: Possible dependency problem
body:
## Describe the bug

Mesh operation fails with a `Process finished with exit code 139 (interrupted by signal 11: SIGSEGV)` when importing a specific set of modules in a particular order.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

Running the following script

```
import dolfin
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from bluemira.builders.plasma import MakeParameterisedPlasma
from bluemira.mesh import meshing
from bluemira.mesh.tools import import_mesh, msh_to_xdmf

# %%[markdown]
# # Create a plasma shape

# %%

params = {
    "R_0": (9.0, "Input"),
    "A": (3.5, "Input"),
}
build_config = {
    "name": "Plasma",
    "class": "MakeParameterisedPlasma",
    "param_class": "bluemira.equilibria.shapes::JohnerLCFS",
    "variables_map": {
        "r_0": "R_0",
        "a": "A",
    },
}
builder = MakeParameterisedPlasma(params, build_config)
plasma = builder().get_component("xz").get_component("LCFS")

plasma.shape.mesh_options = {"lcar": 0.3, "physical_group": "plasma"}
plasma.shape.boundary[0].mesh_options = {"lcar": 0.3, "physical_group": "lcfs"}

# %%[markdown]

# Initialize and create the mesh

# %%

m = meshing.Mesh()
buffer = m(plasma)

# %%[markdown]

# # Convert to xdmf and plot

# %%

msh_to_xdmf("Mesh.msh", dimensions=(0, 2), directory=".", verbose=True)

mesh, boundaries, subdomains, labels = import_mesh(
    "Mesh",
    directory=".",
    subdomains=True,
)
dolfin.plot(mesh)
plt.show()
```

the following error is raised: `Process finished with exit code 139 (interrupted by signal 11: SIGSEGV)`

However, if in the import section, MakeParameterisedPlasma is imported first, i.e.:
```
from bluemira.builders.plasma import MakeParameterisedPlasma
import dolfin
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from bluemira.mesh import meshing
from bluemira.mesh.tools import import_mesh, msh_to_xdmf
```

the run is completed without error.

## Expected behaviour

 Run of the code should be independent of the import order and no errors should be raised.

## Environment (please complete the following information)

- OS: [Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS]
- Version [e.g. 0.0.x]
- Branch (if developing) [develop]

## Additional context

The reported order configurations are just examples of a "bad" and "good" case. Other reordering of such imports can lead to an error (or a successful exit).

title: Bump pybind11-global from 2.9.2 to 2.10.0
body:
Bumps [pybind11-global](https://github.com/pybind/pybind11) from 2.9.2 to 2.10.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pybind11-global's releases.

Version 2.10.0

Removed support for Python 2.7, Python 3.5, and MSVC 2015. Support for MSVC 2017 is limited due to availability of CI runners; we highly recommend MSVC 2019 or 2022 be used. Initial support added for Python 3.11.

New features:

  • py::anyset & py::frozenset were added, with copying (cast) to std::set (similar to set). #3901
  • Support bytearray casting to string. #3707
  • type_caster<std::monostate> was added. std::monostate is a tag type that allows std::variant to act as an optional, or allows default construction of a std::variant holding a non-default constructible type. #3818
  • pybind11::capsule::set_name added to mutate the name of the capsule instance. #3866
  • NumPy: dtype constructor from type number added, accessors corresponding to Python API dtype.num, dtype.byteorder, dtype.flags and dtype.alignment added. #3868

Changes:

  • Python 3.6 is now the minimum supported version. #3688 #3719
  • The minimum version for MSVC is now 2017. #3722
  • Fix issues with CPython 3.11 betas and add to supported test matrix. #3923
  • error_already_set is now safer and more performant, especially for exceptions with long tracebacks, by delaying computation. #1895
  • Improve exception handling in python str bindings. #3826
  • The bindings for capsules now have more consistent exception handling. #3825
  • PYBIND11_OBJECT_CVT and PYBIND11_OBJECT_CVT_DEFAULT macro can now be used to define classes in namespaces other than pybind11. #3797
  • Error printing code now uses PYBIND11_DETAILED_ERROR_MESSAGES instead of requiring NDEBUG, allowing use with release builds if desired. #3913
  • Implicit conversion of the literal 0 to pybind11::handle is now disabled. #4008

Bug fixes:

  • Fix exception handling when pybind11::weakref() fails. #3739
  • module_::def_submodule was missing proper error handling. This is fixed now. #3973
  • The behavior or error_already_set was made safer and the highly opaque "Unknown internal error occurred" message was replaced with a more helpful message. #3982
  • error_already_set::what() now handles non-normalized exceptions correctly. #3971
  • Support older C++ compilers where filesystem is not yet part of the standard library and is instead included in std::experimental::filesystem. #3840
  • Fix -Wfree-nonheap-object warnings produced by GCC by avoiding returning pointers to static objects with return_value_policy::take_ownership. #3946
  • Fix cast from pytype rvalue to another pytype. #3949
  • Ensure proper behavior when garbage collecting classes with dynamic attributes in Python >=3.9. #4051
  • A couple long-standing PYBIND11_NAMESPACE __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) inconsistencies are now fixed (affects only unusual environments). #4043
  • pybind11::detail::get_internals() is now resilient to in-flight Python exceptions. #3981
  • Arrays with a dimension of size 0 are now properly converted to dynamic Eigen matrices (more common in NumPy 1.23). #4038
  • Avoid catching unrelated errors when importing NumPy. #3974

Performance and style:

  • Added an accessor overload of (object &&key) to reference steal the object when using python types as keys. This prevents unnecessary reference count overhead for attr, dictionary, tuple, and sequence look ups. Added additional regression tests. Fixed a performance bug the caused accessor assignments to potentially perform unnecessary copies. #3970
  • Perfect forward all args of make_iterator. #3980
  • Avoid potential bug in pycapsule destructor by adding an error_guard to one of the dtors. #3958
  • Optimize dictionary access in strip_padding for numpy. #3994
  • stl_bind.h bindings now take slice args as a const-ref. #3852
  • Made slice constructor more consistent, and improve performance of some casters by allowing reference stealing. #3845
  • Change numpy dtype from_args method to use const ref. #3878
  • Follow rule of three to ensure PyErr_Restore is called only once. #3872
  • Added missing perfect forwarding for make_iterator functions. #3860
  • Optimize c++ to python function casting by using the rvalue caster. #3966

... (truncated)

title: Bump pybind11 from 2.9.2 to 2.10.0
body:
Bumps [pybind11](https://github.com/pybind/pybind11) from 2.9.2 to 2.10.0.
Release notes

Sourced from pybind11's releases.

Version 2.10.0

Removed support for Python 2.7, Python 3.5, and MSVC 2015. Support for MSVC 2017 is limited due to availability of CI runners; we highly recommend MSVC 2019 or 2022 be used. Initial support added for Python 3.11.

New features:

  • py::anyset & py::frozenset were added, with copying (cast) to std::set (similar to set). #3901
  • Support bytearray casting to string. #3707
  • type_caster<std::monostate> was added. std::monostate is a tag type that allows std::variant to act as an optional, or allows default construction of a std::variant holding a non-default constructible type. #3818
  • pybind11::capsule::set_name added to mutate the name of the capsule instance. #3866
  • NumPy: dtype constructor from type number added, accessors corresponding to Python API dtype.num, dtype.byteorder, dtype.flags and dtype.alignment added. #3868

Changes:

  • Python 3.6 is now the minimum supported version. #3688 #3719
  • The minimum version for MSVC is now 2017. #3722
  • Fix issues with CPython 3.11 betas and add to supported test matrix. #3923
  • error_already_set is now safer and more performant, especially for exceptions with long tracebacks, by delaying computation. #1895
  • Improve exception handling in python str bindings. #3826
  • The bindings for capsules now have more consistent exception handling. #3825
  • PYBIND11_OBJECT_CVT and PYBIND11_OBJECT_CVT_DEFAULT macro can now be used to define classes in namespaces other than pybind11. #3797
  • Error printing code now uses PYBIND11_DETAILED_ERROR_MESSAGES instead of requiring NDEBUG, allowing use with release builds if desired. #3913
  • Implicit conversion of the literal 0 to pybind11::handle is now disabled. #4008

Bug fixes:

  • Fix exception handling when pybind11::weakref() fails. #3739
  • module_::def_submodule was missing proper error handling. This is fixed now. #3973
  • The behavior or error_already_set was made safer and the highly opaque "Unknown internal error occurred" message was replaced with a more helpful message. #3982
  • error_already_set::what() now handles non-normalized exceptions correctly. #3971
  • Support older C++ compilers where filesystem is not yet part of the standard library and is instead included in std::experimental::filesystem. #3840
  • Fix -Wfree-nonheap-object warnings produced by GCC by avoiding returning pointers to static objects with return_value_policy::take_ownership. #3946
  • Fix cast from pytype rvalue to another pytype. #3949
  • Ensure proper behavior when garbage collecting classes with dynamic attributes in Python >=3.9. #4051
  • A couple long-standing PYBIND11_NAMESPACE __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) inconsistencies are now fixed (affects only unusual environments). #4043
  • pybind11::detail::get_internals() is now resilient to in-flight Python exceptions. #3981
  • Arrays with a dimension of size 0 are now properly converted to dynamic Eigen matrices (more common in NumPy 1.23). #4038
  • Avoid catching unrelated errors when importing NumPy. #3974

Performance and style:

  • Added an accessor overload of (object &&key) to reference steal the object when using python types as keys. This prevents unnecessary reference count overhead for attr, dictionary, tuple, and sequence look ups. Added additional regression tests. Fixed a performance bug the caused accessor assignments to potentially perform unnecessary copies. #3970
  • Perfect forward all args of make_iterator. #3980
  • Avoid potential bug in pycapsule destructor by adding an error_guard to one of the dtors. #3958
  • Optimize dictionary access in strip_padding for numpy. #3994
  • stl_bind.h bindings now take slice args as a const-ref. #3852
  • Made slice constructor more consistent, and improve performance of some casters by allowing reference stealing. #3845
  • Change numpy dtype from_args method to use const ref. #3878
  • Follow rule of three to ensure PyErr_Restore is called only once. #3872
  • Added missing perfect forwarding for make_iterator functions. #3860
  • Optimize c++ to python function casting by using the rvalue caster. #3966

... (truncated)

title: Run plotting tests with non-interactive backend
body:
## Linked Issues

Closes #1173 

## Description

Plotting tests are now enabled by default and run with a non-interactive backend. This means we run all the plotting tests on the CI etc., but no interactive windows prevent the execution of subsequent tests. The `--plotting-on` flag still remains, and is used to switch to an interactive backend. The `exec_` method on `QApplication` is mocked before the test suite is run, so no blocking window is opened to display CAD; again this behaviour can be overridden using the `--plotting-on` flag.

Sorry for so many review requests, but this touches almost everything!

I confirm that I have completed the following checks:

- [ ] Tests run locally and pass `pytest tests --reactor`
- [ ] Code quality checks run locally and pass `flake8` and `black .`
- [ ] Documentation built locally and checked `sphinx-build -W documentation/source documentation/build`

title: Bump attrs from 21.4.0 to 22.1.0
body:
Bumps [attrs](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs) from 21.4.0 to 22.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from attrs's releases.

22.1.0

Highlights

The main features of this release are:

  • The departure of Python 2.7 (enjoy your retirement!),
  • and the arrival of Python 3.11.

We had loftier goals feature-wise, but didn't want to block others embracing Python 3.11.

❤️ Huge thanks to my GitHub sponsors, Tidelift subscribers, and Ko-fi buyers! ❤️

None of my projects would exist in their current form without you!

Full Changelog

Backwards-incompatible Changes

  • Python 2.7 is not supported anymore.

    Dealing with Python 2.7 tooling has become too difficult for a volunteer-run project.

    We have supported Python 2 more than 2 years after it was officially discontinued and feel that we have paid our dues. All version up to 21.4.0 from December 2021 remain fully functional, of course. #936

  • The deprecated cmp attribute of attrs.Attribute has been removed. This does not affect the cmp argument to attr.s that can be used as a shortcut to set eq and order at the same time. #939

Changes

  • Instantiation of frozen slotted classes is now faster. #898
  • If an eq key is defined, it is also used before hashing the attribute. #909
  • Added attrs.validators.min_len(). #916
  • attrs.validators.deep_iterable()'s member_validator argument now also accepts a list of validators and wraps them in an attrs.validators.and_(). #925
  • Added missing type stub re-imports for attrs.converters and attrs.filters. #931
  • Added missing stub for attr(s).cmp_using(). #949
  • attrs.validators._in()'s ValueError is not missing the attribute, expected options, and the value it got anymore. #951
  • Python 3.11 is now officially supported. #969
Changelog

Sourced from attrs's changelog.

22.1.0 (2022-07-28)

Backwards-incompatible Changes ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

  • Python 2.7 is not supported anymore.

    Dealing with Python 2.7 tooling has become too difficult for a volunteer-run project.

    We have supported Python 2 more than 2 years after it was officially discontinued and feel that we have paid our dues. All version up to 21.4.0 from December 2021 remain fully functional, of course. [#936](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/936) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/936>_

  • The deprecated cmp attribute of attrs.Attribute has been removed. This does not affect the cmp argument to attr.s that can be used as a shortcut to set eq and order at the same time. [#939](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/939) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/939>_

Changes ^^^^^^^

  • Instantiation of frozen slotted classes is now faster. [#898](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/898) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/898>_
  • If an eq key is defined, it is also used before hashing the attribute. [#909](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/909) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/909>_
  • Added attrs.validators.min_len(). [#916](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/916) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/916>_
  • attrs.validators.deep_iterable()'s member_validator argument now also accepts a list of validators and wraps them in an attrs.validators.and_(). [#925](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/925) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/925>_
  • Added missing type stub re-imports for attrs.converters and attrs.filters. [#931](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/931) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/931>_
  • Added missing stub for attr(s).cmp_using(). [#949](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/949) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/949>_
  • attrs.validators._in()'s ValueError is not missing the attribute, expected options, and the value it got anymore. [#951](https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/951) <https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs/issues/951>_
